doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.35768: Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of $α$-Ta(110), $α$-Ta(111), and metastable $β$-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) at 300-900 $^\circ$C while varying the O$_2$ partial pressure from a $5.5\times10^{-11}$ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to $2.23\times10^{-4}$ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}\leq4.8\times10^{-6}$ to 19). Without added oxygen, $α$-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O$_2$ pressure of only $2.5\times10^{-9}$ Torr ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}=2.2\times10^{-4}$), $α$-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 $^\circ$C, decreasing to 65% at 900 $^\circ$C. Substantial $β$-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 $^\circ$C and disappearing at 900 $^\circ$C. The apparent $β$(001)/$α$(110) selection energy of $1.07\pm0.16$ eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.
doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.34924: We investigate native defects and their impact on the electronic structure of Td-MoTe2 and graphene/Td-MoTe2 van der Waals heterostructures using scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy. STM reveals a high density of circular, hollow surface defects that we attribute to Te vacancies. STS on pristine MoTe2 shows semimetallic, V-shaped dI/dV spectra with subtle low-energy states. The vacancies suppress the tunnelling conductance below the Fermi level without introducing new sharp defect-related resonances, consistent with a vacancy-induced redistribution of Mo-Te spectral weight rather than the appearance of new electronic states. In the heterostructure, graphene preserves these MoTe2 fingerprints with no noticeable graphene doping or charge transfer. Our results demonstrate that isolated native Te vacancies act as spectroscopically weak perturbations to the low-energy electronic structure of graphene. The graphene overlayer further screens their impact on the electronic structure, making graphene/Td-MoTe2 heterostructures intrinsically tolerant to such interface defects.
doi:10.1002/smll.76358: ABSTRACT Plasmonic metals are considered a promising approach for enhancing the reactivity of solar‐driven photocatalysts when used as co‐catalytic nanostructures. However, optimizing the energy conversion efficiency is challenging because it requires precise control of the light‐matter interactions at the nanoscale. In this work, we present metamaterial photocatalyst sheets that combine titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) thin films and plasmonic metal nanodisks arranged in periodic arrays. Silver (Ag), gold (Au), platinum (Pt), and palladium (Pd) were used as nanodisk metals. We tested our photocatalyst sheets for generating solar fuels hydrogen (H 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) from carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) using steamed water (H 2 O) mixed with isopropyl alcohol (IPA) as a sacrificial agent under broadband (UV–vis–NIR) light exposure. Our Pt/TiO 2 and Pd/TiO 2 photocatalysts achieved gas product rates of 4.37 µmol cm −2 h −1 for H 2 and 0.42 µmol cm −2 h −1 for CH 4 . The fabrication process flow is based on standard semiconductor fabrication methods, showing its potential for large‐scale applications.
doi:10.1021/acsami.6c18985: We report on the controlled growth and interface engineering of high-quality WSe2 monolayers on Au(111) using ambient-pressure chemical vapor deposition (CVD) combined with comprehensive surface-sensitive characterization in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV). The as-grown films exhibit a selenium buffer layer, which enables the formation of a weakly coupled WSe2 phase at the metal interface, as revealed by scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED). Annealing in UHV removes the selenium buffer layer and leads to the emergence of a pronounced moiré superstructure and a transition toward a strongly coupled WSe2 phase. Furthermore, this transformation is accompanied by pronounced modifications of the electronic structure, including phase-dependent changes in the valence band structure observed by angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES), a hybridization-induced metallization measured by scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), and a significant decrease in the work function determined by field emission resonance (FER) and ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy (UPS). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm strong WSe2-Au hybridization and the presence of the mid-gap states for the strongly coupled phase, whereas the Se8 buffer layer weakens the interaction of WSe2 with Au, so that its electronic structure is close to that for the freestanding system. Our results demonstrate that growth-induced interface chemistry provides a powerful handle to tune the electronic coupling in WSe2/Au(111), establishing a direct link between interfacial structure and electronic properties in metal-transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) interfaces.
doi:10.1002/admi.70713: ABSTRACT Adsorption of proteins and other biomolecules on stainless steel and other functional metallic surfaces is a key interfacial phenomenon in food processing environments, leading to progressive surface accumulation of organic residues. Their presence can impair the material performance, promote microbial adhesion, complicate cleaning procedures, and ultimately create significant hygiene challenges. In this study, UV–vis fluorescence spectroscopy was evaluated for its suitability in monitoring the adsorption of plant‐derived biomolecules on AISI 316L stainless steel surfaces, using rice protein concentrate in artificial tap water, both in the presence and absence of stearic acid and NaCl. Instrumental parameters were optimized based on multi‐Gaussian peak deconvolution using Bayesian Information Criterion evaluation. This approach enabled robust resolution of overlapping spectral features and improved sensitivity in complex matrices. Fluorescence peak shifts and intensity variations were analyzed to probe protein–alloy surface interactions, providing diagnostic indicators of protein‐induced spectral changes and proposed conformational transitions resulting from protein adsorption. The results demonstrate that fluorescence spectroscopy is a valuable technique for monitoring interfacial protein adsorption and residue accumulation on stainless steel under food‐processing conditions. Overall, the findings provide insights relevant to hygiene control strategies and the optimization of material performance in food‐processing systems.
doi:10.1007/s00784-026-07231-w: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the effects of a phytosphingosine-enriched toothpaste (PET) versus a commercial toothpaste on dental enamel using in vitro and in situ approaches. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In vitro, bovine enamel specimens were assigned to one of three brushing agents, artificial saliva, Colgate Total 12, or PET and subjected to simulated brushing (40, 280, 600, and 1,200 cycles), each representing the estimated brushing exposure for 1, 7, 15, and 30 days, respectively. Each group of specimens were evaluated at all time points throughout the 30-day period. Surface roughness and microhardness were measured. In situ, 14 volunteers used appliances containing enamel samples, brushed with the same toothpastes. Roughness, microhardness, and biofilm accumulation were assessed. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) characterized enamel surfaces post-treatment. RESULTS: In vitro, PET showed lower surface roughness than saliva at 7 days (p 0.05). However, PET significantly reduced biofilm compared to saliva (p < 0.05). AFM revealed smooth surfaces with both PET and the commercial product. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated the PHS-enriched toothpaste did not adversely affect enamel integrity and resulted in significantly lower biofilm coverage on enamel, suggesting its potential for use in preventive oral care formulations. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study suggests that a phytosphingosine-enriched toothpaste is a promising option for preventive dentistry, as it resulted in lower biofilm accumulation on enamel without compromising enamel integrity. Given the central role of biofilm in the development of caries and periodontal disease, these findings provide scientific support for the future development of safer oral hygiene products as alternatives to conventional agents such as triclosan and chlorhexidine.
doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010878/v1: The mechanical behavior of DNA origami nanostructures (DONs) is governed by both design parameters and ionic environment, yet their coupled effects remain poorly understood. Here, atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based contour analysis is used to quantify the persistence length (Lp), contour length (Lc), and end-to-end distance (Ree) of DON six-helix bundles (6HBs) with different staple crossover densities. Non-ligated and ligated 6HBs are compared in the presence of MgCl2 and SrCl2, while oxDNA simulations employing implicit monovalent salt screening help distinguish design-dependent from ion-specific effects. While providing comparable diffuse electrostatic screening, Mg2+ and Sr2+ interact differently with DONs and produce distinct design-dependent mechanical responses. For non-ligated 6HBs, lower Lp values are obtained in Sr2+ than in Mg2+, with the magnitude of the difference depending on crossover density. Paired Ree-versus-Lc analysis further indicates greater bending heterogeneity in Sr2+. In the presence of both cations, ligation may lead to an increase or a decrease in Lp depending on crossover density. Simulations reproduce the opposite ligation responses of the two designs but not the Mg2+-associated behavior, supporting an additional contribution from specific divalent cation interactions. These results establish crossover density, backbone continuity, and cation species as coupled variables whose interplay controls DON mechanics.
doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.31924: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models and spatial resolution. Here we demonstrate a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model that establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit. We discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from a pinned state directly at the channel-dielectric interface of an organic transistor, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics that contradict models based on substrate patterning. This non-destructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final configuration opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.
doi:10.1021/jacs.6c09065: Abstract High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remain concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO3 perovskite electrodes, La1–xSrx(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 with x = 0 and 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipet-probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant (kd0 cm/s), transfer coefficient (α), and proton reaction order (b) for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A-site substitution (30% Sr2+) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.
doi:10.64898/2026.10.19.760138: Abstract AFM experiments can now produce hundreds of frames per session and this rises to thousands in the case of video-rate high-speed AFM, but every image must still be levelled to remove tilt, bowing and line noise before it can be measured. Current automatic routines rely on user-chosen masks and parameters that work for some sample types but fail on others, so levelling often remains a manual, subjective bottleneck. Here, we present two U-Net models developed using machine learning for levelling AFM images without altering the sample topography. MLMask segments features so that they are excluded from conventional plane and line background fits, and MLBackground predicts the noise and artifact background directly, which is then subtracted. Both were trained on 2,001 experimental images from multiple instruments and sample types, using manually levelled images as ground truth. On 164 unseen images, MLMask routines brought 70–80% of images below a mean squared error of 0.1 relative to manual levelling, compared with 60–70% for the best multi-plane method, with a lower mean error (0.1–0.15 vs 0.15–0.3), and both models significantly outperformed fourteen classical routines ( p < 0.01). Applied frame by frame, the models process 512 × 512 pixel HS-AFM movies at 4.7 frames s −1 . We provide afMLevel as an openly-available package for the use of other researchers. By removing the need to choose levelling parameters image by image, this package together with its models and paired training data, provides a foundation for automated AFM analysis pipelines.
doi:10.1021/acselectrochem.6c00252: Abstract Identifying the onset potential at which perovskite oxide catalysts begin to undergo near-surface changes under oxygen evolution (OER) polarization is critical for separating intrinsic electrocatalytic behavior from evolving surface chemistries. Here, early surface modification was tracked during the first anodic sweep in 0.1 M KOH using electrochemical friction force microscopy (EC-FFM) under a low normal load of 5 nN to avoid mechanically induced removal of the reacted layer. Epitaxial La0.6Sr0.4BO3–δ thin films (B = Co or Fe) were probed while recording cyclic voltammograms (CV). Onset potentials were extracted from friction (EF), topographic roughening (ER), and the CV current response (Ej) using a consistent tangent method. For both catalysts, friction changes preceded morphology changes, with EF occurring 0.26 ± 0.02 V earlier than ER for LSCO and 0.13 ± 0.05 V earlier than ER for LSFO (all potentials vs. RHE) at 10 mV s–1. Based on the established involvement of OH-derived surface species in alkaline OER mechanisms and the demonstrated sensitivity of electrochemical friction to adsorbate-induced changes of the interface, EF is assigned to the onset of a friction-detectable interfacial modification that is consistent with potential-induced hydroxide adsorption/surface hydroxylation, whereas ER marks the onset of morphologically resolvable surface restructuring. The material-dependent ΔE = ER – EF separation therefore describes the potential interval between the initial friction-detectable interfacial modification and its morphological expression.
doi:10.3390/antiox15101363: Oxidative stress and industrial water pollution represent critical global challenges that demand the development of sustainable, multitarget remediation platforms. This study addresses the existing knowledge gap regarding the modulation of green-synthesized iron nanostructures by secondary transition metals through the fabrication of silver–iron (AgFe), cobalt–iron (CoFe), and copper–iron (CuFe) bimetallic oxide formulations using Anacardium occidentale L. pericarp extracts as dual-functional reducing and capping agents. Characterization was performed using UV-Vis, DLS, AFM, Raman, FTIR, and XRD techniques to elucidate their structural properties. Our results demonstrate that phytochemicals within the agro-industrial byproduct facilitated the formation of stable, spherical bimetallic oxide nanostructures. The CuFe formulation exhibited the highest catalytic activity, achieving 99.1% conversion/reduction of 4-nitrophenol within 6.3 min. Furthermore, all bimetallic oxide formulations demonstrated superior radical scavenging capacity, as evidenced by FRAP/DPPH assays, confirming the synergistic effect of the secondary metals on electron-transfer kinetics. These findings indicate that the integration of secondary metals significantly enhances the performance of biogenic iron-based oxide nanoparticles. Consequently, this study establishes an eco-friendly protocol for the production of bimetallic oxide nanostructures, providing a robust, dual-purpose platform for both environmental remediation and advanced biomedical antioxidant applications.
doi:10.1063/5.0349056: One of the most promising building blocks for the development of spin qubits, single-photon sources, and quantum sensors at room temperature, as well as 2D ultraviolet light-emitting diodes, is defect color centers in 2D hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). However, a significant requirement for the realization of such devices toward scalable technologies is the deterministic localization of hBN color centers. Here, we demonstrate a novel approach to the localization of hBN color center emission by using patterned dielectric layers grown on graphene via atomic layer deposition (ALD). While color center emission is quenched within areas where hBN is transferred directly on graphene due to charge transfer, it is maintained where hBN is transferred on micrometer-sized Al2O3 pillars, which act as barriers to charge transfer. Importantly, our approach allows for device architectures where graphene layers are used as top and bottom electrodes for the application of vertical electric fields, such as for carrier injection in electroluminescent devices, Stark shifting of color center emission, and charge state control of defect color centers. Furthermore, the use of ALD to grow dielectric layers directly on graphene allows for the control of tunnel barrier thicknesses with atomic layer precision, which is crucial for many of these device applications. Our work represents an important step toward the realization of a wide range of scalable device applications based on the deterministic localization of electrically controlled hBN color centers.
doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010683/v1: Realising chemically programmable two-dimensional magnetic materials is a major challenge in the development of next-generation quantum technologies. Layered magnetic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide an attractive platform because their reticular design enables systematic control over composition, topology, and magnetic interactions while offering the possibility of exfoliation into atomically thin nanosheets. Here, we investigate the layered S = 1/2 kagome MOF, Cu 3 (CO 3 ) 2 ( bipy ) 6 · 2 ClO 4 , whose bulk magnetic structure is most consistently described by ferromagnetic kagome layers that are ferromagnetically correlated to adjacent ones. We develop a micromechanical Scotch tape exfoliation strategy capable of producing few-layer nanosheets and combine synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) to demonstrate that the Cu 2+ oxidation state and ferromagnetic behaviour are retained following exfoliation. By showing that magnetic functionality is preserved in the exfoliated kagome MOF nanosheets, this work establishes the promise of layered magnetic MOFs as tuneable platforms for low-dimensional quantum magnetism and provides an important experimental route toward realising the archetypal S = 1/2 kagome magnet in the two-dimensional limit.
doi:10.4121/abe01e5b-ad67-44a0-a9bb-fbb6: This dataset contains scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS) measurements of Bi(110) on a Ge(111) substrate. This dataset contains raw data, step-by-step manipulated data and analysis scripts. Each file is labelled using the figure number it corresponds to. The STM topography images can be opened using the open-source Gwyddion tool (https://gwyddion.net/). Each topography file contains both the raw and final version of the image. The STS curves are stored in a plain-text csv format. The scripts are Python 3 Jupyter notebooks. Some scripts make use of the Pingwyn library for Python 3. The source code and installation instructions can be found at https://gitlab.utwente.nl/pin/pingwyn.
doi:10.1021/acsanm.6c03660: Abstract Properties of transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers are strongly modified when interfaced with metals rather than weakly interacting substrates such as SiO2. For monolayer MoS2 on Au, the vibrational spectrum serves as a sensitive probe of substrate-driven charge transfer, strain, and hybridization. However, how these interactions evolve in response to roughness-induced changes in Au surface morphology remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate monolayer MoS2 exfoliated onto Au films with varying surface roughness and show that its properties are governed by the balance between regions that conform to the underlying Au surface and regions that remain locally suspended. Correlative analyses combining atomic force microscopy, Raman/photoluminescence spectroscopy, and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that increasing substrate roughness hinders conformal contact between MoS2 and Au, promotes the formation of locally suspended regions, and enhances tensile strain in the monolayer. Furthermore, we demonstrate that incorporating a Pt adhesion layer yields exceptionally smooth Au surfaces, enabling efficient exfoliation even on ultrathin Au films and providing a cost-effective route toward large-area monolayer preparation. These findings establish interfacial morphology as a key parameter governing the mechanical, vibrational, and optical properties of monolayer MoS2 and provide practical design guidelines for engineering metal−2D material interfaces for (opto)electronic, catalytic, and sensing applications.
doi:10.1016/j.diamond.2026.114302: The ability to remove surface defects of diamond by dry etching methods is of high importance for applications that make use of shallow color centers in diamond. Here, we present an atomic layer etching process, making use of oxygen as dosing gas and argon as etching gas, in order to achieve controlled etching of the surface without creating additional defects by sputtering. We demonstrate a process window, where quasi-self-limiting atomic layer etching takes place with an etch per cycle of (1.909 ± 0.004) Å/cycle, corresponding to about 2 atomic layers of the {100} oriented diamond sample. The process is able to reduce the rms surface roughness down to (0.15 ± 0.01) nm. Furthermore, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicates only a small amount of sp 2 bonded carbon on the diamond surface after the atomic layer etching process.
doi:10.64898/2026.10.13.758739: Abstract Understanding the mechanisms underlying substrate recognition and selectivity is essential for developing new biotechnological applications of carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs). Many members of CBM family 2 (CBM2) prefer binding to crystalline substrates and show diverse substrate specificities despite sharing similar folds. We show here that CBM2 specificity cannot be rationalized solely based on sequence and fold. Rather, specific binding of CBM2s to crystalline surfaces depends on a balance of topological complementarity, hydrophobic dehydration, and hydrogen-bonding interactions. We compare the binding modes of Sc CBM2 and Ba CBM2 on cellulose, chitin, and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) with respect to protein and substrate properties. Using MD simulations and NMR, we explore the CBMs’ surface topology, hydration, solvent accessibility, and electrostatics. The results indicate that the two CBMs may bind to crystalline substrates in opposite orientations, and that the interplay between hydrophobic and π-stacking interactions along the aromatic triad and hydrogen-bonding interactions on either side determines their orientation. We further show that higher water density at the aromatic triad correlates with higher substrate affinity. Lastly, we probe the interaction dynamics of Ba CBM2 with PET nanoparticles and the monomer bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) using NMR relaxation and solvent paramagnetic relaxation enhancement (sPRE) experiments, revealing a mixture of transient, low-population states involved in PET binding. These insights clarify the interplay among factors that drive CBM2 substrate recognition and highlight the importance of evaluating surface hydration and protein dynamics in future CBM2 studies.
doi:10.3390/ma19204363: This study investigated the electrochemical protection provided by amorphous hafnium thin films deposited on austenitic stainless steel by atomic layer deposition technology that guarantees control over the physicochemical properties of deposited coatings and processes repeatability. Furthermore, ALD enables conformal coating of three-dimensional shapes. The corrosion resistance of these coatings was evaluated under conditions simulating physiological environments, using potentiodynamic polarization and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Furthermore, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and atomic force microscopy were employed to analyze the chemical stability, surface condition, and morphology of the films prior to and following electrochemical testing. Potentiodynamic polarization tests demonstrated that uncoated SS316L provided insufficient corrosion resistivity, whereas samples coated with ALD-grown hafnium dioxide thin films possessed barrier properties, exhibited a pronounced passive region and a reduction in anodic and cathodic current densities by up to three orders of magnitude. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results further verified the development of a compact, highly resistive dielectric interface. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis demonstrated that the films exhibited chemical stability following corrosion. SEM images showed that after electrochemical tests on stainless steel, significant surface degradation was observed, whereas the hafnium dioxide-coated surfaces remained unchanged. The findings suggested that films with a thickness of ≈100 nm act as effective barriers to corrosive ions. These results highlight the potential of ALD-deposited amorphous hafnium dioxide thin films as protective coatings against corrosion and present promising prospects for future biomedical applications.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11261172/v1: Abstract Cold-sprayed copper is a promising additive manufacturing material for a range of applications, including used nuclear fuel containers. Under aggressive dilute nitric acid conditions, it exhibits preferential corrosion associated with the oxide network incorporated during fabrication, a phenomenon that remains poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate the mechanism of this preferential corrosion by varying the presence of dissolved oxygen and the concentrations of copper ions and chloride. By exploiting the inhibitive effect of chloride on nitrate reduction, we show that nitrate reduction is necessary before the initiation of preferential attack at the oxide-rich particle-particle boundaries can occur. In addition, dissolved copper ions substantially accelerate corrosion, providing direct experimental evidence for their proposed catalytic role. Material loss is ultimately dominated by particle detachment following preferential dissolution along the oxide network. These findings provide new insight into the corrosion mechanism of cold-sprayed copper in dilute nitric acid and indicate that preferential corrosion is specific to nitrate-containing, chloride-free environments.
doi:10.1038/s41417-026-01085-w: The astounding success of mRNA empowers the diverse application of mRNA therapeutics in multiple genetic disorders. Besides the vaccines, the rational design of mRNA drugs has been explored widely to target the undruggable gene therapy for managing cancer. Restoration of the p53 tumor suppressor gene via introducing foreign p53-mRNA therapeutics may inhibit the growth and development of tumors. Since the development of mRNA transporting vehicles, liposome-based nanoparticles are the mainstay and are widely used in several ex vivo and clinical studies. But the delivery of mRNA outside the immune cells and hepatocytes for protein replacement therapy through systemic administartion is very limited and requires additional optimization. Here, we modified classical LNP (lipid nanoparticles) with SSNs (strontium sulfite nanoparticles) and complexed the LNP with p53 mRNA to improve the delivery efficiency of p53 mRNA. We assumed that restoration of p53 function in breast tumor cells might improve antitumor efficacy against breast cancer. We screened the SSNs-LNP to get the favorable physicochemical properties and to improve the delivery efficiency. The SSNs-LNP showed a threefold increase of luciferase gene expression in breast cancer cell lines compared to the classical LNP. In the animal model, the SSNs-LNP improved the biological stability and tumor targeting efficiency and restored the expression of p53, resulting in a significant reduction of tumor volume. Thus, we anticipate that the hybrid SSNs-LNP particles could be a translatable nanocarrier system in transporting mRNA drugs for the treatment of cancers.
doi:10.1111/jmi.70191: Since its introduction 40 years ago, atomic force microscopy (AFM) has transformed nanoscale imaging across the physical and life sciences. In biology, AFM has provided unprecedented insights into nanoscale biomolecular organisation under near-physiological conditions, revealing structures and interactions inaccessible to many conventional approaches. However, biological function is inherently dynamic, and understanding molecular mechanisms requires moving beyond static structural snapshots towards direct observation of processes across multiple spatial and temporal scales. In this review, we discuss emerging approaches that are extending the capabilities of AFM beyond traditional imaging, pushing the limits of temporal resolution, spatial precision, quantitative measurement, and data analysis. We highlight advances in speed that enable direct visualisation of molecular dynamics, approaches for sub-millisecond measurements, methods that overcome conventional resolution limits, and computational approaches that enhance image analysis, automation, and information extraction from complex datasets. Together, these developments are transforming AFM from a technique focused primarily on high-resolution structural imaging into a platform for dynamic, quantitative, and high-throughput investigation of biological systems. Finally, we consider how these advances may shape the next 40 years of AFM, enable autonomous measurements and reveal biological mechanisms across previously inaccessible spatial and temporal scales.
doi:10.1021/jacs.6c08825: Nonbenzenoid topologies offer a compelling strategy to tailor the electronic properties of low-dimensional carbon materials. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis of a nonalternant polymer incorporating a [7-5-5] cyclopenta[c,d]azulene (CPA) motif on Au(111) via thermally induced Ullmann coupling. Bond-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy confirms the robustness of the [7-5-5] framework. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy, together with dI/dV mapping supported by density functional theory calculations, reveals a remarkable narrow polymeric bandgap of 1.5 eV. The electronic structure is governed by the intramolecular charge transfer from the heptagonal ring to the adjacent fused pentagonal rings, resulting in a pronounced dipole moment despite being composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen. Aromaticity analyses indicate the coexistence of locally aromatic and slightly antiaromatic regions, highlighting the intrinsic electronic frustration associated with the nonalternant topology. These findings demonstrate how the controlled incorporation of [7-5-5] motifs enables the rational bandgap engineering in carbon-based polymers and expands the scope of nonbenzenoid design in on-surface synthesis.
doi:10.1016/j.colsurfb.2026.116258: The GM1 oligosaccharide β-Gal-(1-3)-β-GalNAc-(1-4)-[α-Neu5Ac-(2-3)]-β-Gal-(1-4)-Glc (OligoGM1) represents the soluble, bioactive portion of GM1 ganglioside and recapitulates many of its trophic, protective, and restorative effects. Our previous proteomic studies on OligoGM1-treated neuroblastoma cells revealed alterations in endocytic trafficking and extracellular vesicles (EVs) biogenesis suggesting a potential role for OligoGM1 in modulating EV biogenesis. Here, we apply a multi-technique biophysical platform to investigate the physico-chemical properties and functionality of EVs released by murine neuroblastoma Neuro2a cells, treated with OligoGM1. We show that OligoGM1 treatment slightly shifts to lower values the EVs' size population distribution and increases their relative lipid content, accompanied by a higher proportion of membrane-associated proteins. Our analysis further indicates that OligoGM1-treated cells release EVs with altered bilayer structural parameters, including increased apparent membrane thickness, consistent with a modified distribution of lipid/protein contributions within the adopted membrane model. Functional characterization using biomimetic model membranes indicates that EVs from treated and untreated cells differ in protein insertion and lipid exchange efficiency, pointing to distinct membrane-interaction modes relevant to downstream cellular interactions. Overall, these findings suggest that OligoGM1 reshapes the molecular architecture and biophysical behaviour of Neuro2a-derived EVs, providing membrane-level fingerprints that may be relevant for future studies of EV-cell interactions in neurodegenerative models.
doi:10.1002/admi.70700: ABSTRACT Blister formation in thin polymer films represents a localized delamination instability whereby interfacial failure leads to out‐of‐plane deformation of the supported film. It is relevant to coating failure, adhesion control, and directed surface patterning. Photoresponsive azopolymer films provide a unique model system, since mechanical stresses can be generated and tuned remotely by light. Here, we investigate blister formation in substrate‐supported azopolymer films immersed in aqueous environments under spontaneous and optically excited conditions. We show that spontaneous blistering occurs via a complex interplay between diffusion‐limited solvent transport, swelling, capillarity, poroelastic solvent uptake, and osmotic effects, and remains fully reversible upon drying. In contrast, light‐induced structuring is stable after solvent removal, indicating irreversible interfacial reconfiguration. We further demonstrate that linearly polarized light induces pronounced anisotropic deformation in both pre‐existing and newly formed blisters. This anisotropy can be understood within the orientation‐based theory of azobenzene polymer deformation, where chromophore reorientation generates anisotropic active stresses in the delaminated blister and surrounding adhered film. Together with adhesion and geometric constraints, this produces stress redistribution in a curved shell, leading to symmetry breaking and elliptical deformation governed by nonlinear shell mechanics. Overall, we provide a unified framework for swelling‐ and light‐driven interfacial instabilities in azopolymer films.
doi:10.1007/s10853-026-13831-4: A series of manganese-doped ZnO/SiO 2 nanocomposites was studied to establish the structure-property relationships governing visible-light photocatalysis and to assess whether digital colorimetry, chemometrics and machine learning can provide rapid, nondestructive composition control for doped semiconductor/support systems, using the antiviral drug lopinavir as a model pollutant. The novelty lies in coupling machine learning, chemometrics-supported spectroscopy, and digital colorimetry with conventional characterization to enable rapid, nondestructive compositional quality control of this doped oxide/support system.Nanocomposites containing 3, 6, and 9 mmol of Mn–ZnO per gram of SiO 2 were prepared by a wet chemical route followed by thermal treatment at 600 °C. They were characterized by X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy with AI-assisted image segmentation, nitrogen adsorption–desorption, atomic force microscopy, UV-visible spectroscopy and photoluminescence. Digital images were classified using convolutional neural network (Inception v3) embeddings combined with a support vector machine, and infrared spectra (FTIR and IR-ATR) were modeled by principal component analysis and NIPALS regression.Hexagonal wurtzite ZnO formed, with crystallite sizes of 27.7–31.0 nm. Changes in the Raman A 1 (LO) mode were consistent with defect-related lattice distortion, including contributions from oxygen vacancy- and zinc-interstitial-related states. The predominantly mesoporous solids exhibited specific surface areas of 110–160 m 2 g −1 and enhanced visible-light absorption with defect-mediated photoluminescence. The classification pipeline accurately discriminated the samples, and IR-ATR provided improved compositional predictions compared with conventional FTIR. The most active composite, 9-Mn–ZnO/SiO 2 , removed 96 % of lopinavir within 1 h under visible light ( k 1 = 0.0465 min −1 ), with • OH and O 2 −• implicated as the dominant reactive species and stable performance over four reuse cycles.This integrated approach provides mechanistic insight into structure-property relationships and practical, non-destructive quality-control tools for visible-light-active doped metal oxide/support photocatalysts.
doi:10.1088/1402-4896/aeb3c0: Abstract Gold nitride (GN) phases were synthesized using cold nitrogen plasma with N 2 + ions of approximately 800 eV energy at a fluence of 7.5 × 10 14 ions cm −2 . X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of AuN 2 and Au 3 N phases alongside pristine Au. The lattice constants of pristine Au, AuN 2 and Au 3 N found to be a Au = 4.079 ± 0.004 Å, a AuN2 = 4.197 ± 0.004 Å, and a Au3N = 4.024 ± 0.004 Å respectively. The lattice value shows good agreement with the reported values. The fractal dimension, D f of the crystallite interfaces, calculated from XRD, was found to be 2.03 for AuN 2 and 1.94 for Au 3 N. Experimental Raman shifts at 438.0 ± 0.4 cm −1 and 1129.1 ± 0.3 cm −1 matched well with theoretical predictions for the vibrational bands of AuN 2 and Au 3 N. Additionally, the fractal dimension ( D f = 2.48) calculated from Raman scattering corresponded to the interfacial dimension of voids created during synthesis, which matched the grain boundary interface. Morphological analysis revealed particle sizes of GN materials ranging from 20–30 nm, grain sizes from 80–500 nm, and void sizes from 100–300 nm. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM)-based fractal analysis yielded a D f value of 2.4, indicating the interface dimension of grain boundaries and voids. The fractal structural data obtained from x-ray technique, Raman spectroscopy, SEM, and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy showed good agreement.
doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.18251: Large-area molecular junctions combining photochromic and redox-active functionalities provide an attractive platform for controlling charge transport by light. In this work, we study Au/DAEVIO/Ti/Au molecular junctions incorporated with electro-grafted layers of diarylethene-viologen with thicknesses of 12-16 nm. In the initial OFF state, the junctions exhibit low current densities and strong rectification, with a rectification ratio of 300 at 1V. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal a thermally assisted contribution at higher temperatures and a much weaker temperature dependence below 160-180K, consistent with multistep charge transport through molecular and/or interfacial states rather than direct coherent tunneling across the entire molecular layer. Under continuous in situ 385 nm irradiation, the electrical response is strongly and asymmetrically modified. The current density at +1V increases by a factor of 200, while the negative-bias current is only weakly modified, reducing the rectification ratio from 300 to 2. Illumination also produces a nonzero short-circuit current density of + 0.006mA cm-2 and an open-circuit voltage of -0.45V. These results indicate that irradiation simultaneously modifies molecular charge transport and generates a measurable photoelectric response. This behavior is consistent with light-induced changes in electronic coupling associated with DAE photocyclization, combined with photoinduced charge generation and field-dependent charge separation involving the redox-active viologen units and asymmetric electrode interfaces.
doi:10.1002/ejic.70341: The controlled construction of interwoven molecular architectures via metal coordination represents a promising strategy for the development of ordered, interwoven, two‐dimensional (2D) materials. Here, we report a bottom‐up approach to probe the relationship between molecular symmetry and interfacial 2D polymerization behavior. Two amphiphilic heteroleptic osmium(II) terpyridine complexes were designed that incorporate aldehyde and amine functionalities, asymmetric complex ( 1 ), capable of forming two imine bonds, and a symmetric analog with four reactive sites ( 2 ). Langmuir–Blodgett isotherms, Brewster angle microscopy confirmed monolayer formation. In noncontact atomic force microscopy images 1 produced discrete oligomeric aggregates, while 2 yielded extended, chain‐like polymeric structures with high surface coverage. X‐ray photoelectronic spectroscopy measurements supported the presence of polymers as a product of imine condensation. Density functional theory calculations of 1 and its dimer and tetramer were performed to assess the stability of motifs relevant to the supramolecular structures observed. Comparison of the oligomers indicates a slight thermodynamic preference for chain‐like growth over crosslinking. Although these calculations are limited, the intrinsic bias toward linear linkages is consistent with atomic force microscopy data. Together, these results suggest polymer formation through imine condensation on the water–air interface, yielding kinetically favored chain formation and expanded 2D connectivity.
doi:10.1016/j.cejgas.2026.100147: In the present work, alkaline Suaeda monoica biochar (BTBC) and its CoFe₂O₄-modified composite (FCB) were synthesized and comparatively evaluated for Congo red (CR) adsorption from aqueous solutions. The incorporation of CoFe₂O₄ significantly enhanced the adsorption performance of biochar, with FCB exhibiting substantially higher adsorption capacity and faster kinetics than BTBC under varying conditions of contact time, adsorbent dosage, initial dye concentration, temperature, and pH. Both BTBC and FCB showed the highest adsorption at pH 2, 5 mg, 250 ppm, 60 °C. Kinetic studies showed that CR adsorption onto FCB followed the pseudo-second-order model, indicating surface-controlled adsorption with an equilibrium time of 90 min. Equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir isotherm (q max = 1665 mg g −1 ), confirming high-affinity monolayer adsorption by FCB. Thermodynamic analysis revealed that the adsorption process is endothermic and spontaneous, with ΔH° = 17.75 kJ mol −1 . The superior adsorption performance of FCB is attributed to increased active site availability, enhanced surface heterogeneity, and stronger electrostatic interactions resulting from CoFe₂O₄ incorporation. Artificial neural network (ANN) modelling using Levenberg–Marquardt and Bayesian regularization algorithms demonstrated excellent predictive accuracy for adsorption capacity and removal efficiency under diverse experimental conditions. Monte Carlo simulation confirmed π-π stacking as the dominant mechanism for CR adsorption onto FCB. Regeneration studies confirmed the excellent stability of FCB, retaining adsorption capacities exceeding 1000 mg g −1 after five adsorption–desorption cycles. Overall, FCB emerges as an efficient and reusable adsorbent for CR removal from wastewater.
doi:10.1016/j.mtchem.2026.104093: Two-dimensional (2D) materials have attracted growing interest in applications as adsorbent due to their high surface-to-volume ratio and tunable properties. However, randomly stacked 2D structures often suffer from restricted reactant diffusion and limited access to active sites, resulting in suboptimal adsorption performance. In contrast, orderly stacked 2D frameworks can facilitate efficient charge transfer and provide well-defined reaction pathways. Inspired by the concept of graphene organic frameworks (GOFs), we report the synthesis of a 2D gallium oxyhydroxide (GaOOH) framework coordinated by organic ligands via a facile hydrothermal method. Three ligands, including benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid (BTC), benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (BDC), and benzene-1,3,5-triphenyl triboronic acid (TBA), are explored for framework formation. Among them, the GaOOH-BTC material exhibits significantly enhanced surface area, porosity, and a notably shifted conduction band edge compared to randomly stacked GaOOH. As a proof-of-concept, the GaOOH-BTC framework demonstrates outstanding adsorption efficiency, achieving 92% removal of Trypan Blue dye under visible light within 120 min, with excellent repeatability. In contrast, the randomly stacked GaOOH shows only 56.5% removal under the same conditions. The enhanced performance is attributed to the precise stacking, increased BET surface area, favorable valence band edge, and the availability of carboxylate functional groups in the framework. This work introduces 2D GaOOH frameworks as promising, thermally stable alternatives to GOFs for efficient adsorptive pollutant removal applications.
doi:10.1016/j.compscitech.2026.111885: Carbon fibre-reinforced polymer composites rely on efficient stress transfer across the fibre-matrix interphase. Yet, real carbon fibre surfaces exhibit nanoscale roughness and vacancy disorder rarely captured in molecular dynamics (MD) models, which typically assume a pristine graphitic surface. This is particularly limiting for thermoplastic matrices such as poly(ether ether ketone) (PEEK), which lack functional groups capable of covalent crosslinking and rely primarily on π - π interactions with the fibre surface, making surface morphology a key determinant of interfacial performance. Here, a stochastic, Perlin-noise-based defect-generation framework is developed to produce graphene-based reinforcements with spatially correlated vacancy defects, motivated by the nanoscale roughness observed via SEM and high-speed AFM characterisation of IM7-GP carbon fibre. The resulting defective reinforcements show progressive degradation in elastic properties, with Young’s and shear moduli falling over 80% from pristine to the highest defect threshold, consistent with loss of lattice continuity. Nine stacked configurations were combined with an experimentally validated PEEK matrix to isolate the effect of surface-vacancy morphology on interfacial shear stress (ISS). The defect-free interphase yields composites with an ISS of 63 ± 4 MPa, while low-to-moderate vacancy fractions produce no significant change. In contrast, large, spatially connected vacancy clusters increase ISS by 37 − 44 %, a trend confirmed across two pull-out rates, indicating ISS is controlled by mechanical anchoring of PEEK chains within the vacancy network during pull-out. These results show that the framework generates physically meaningful defect morphologies without an annealing step, and demonstrate that vacancy architecture influences interfacial performance, guiding carbon fibre surface design in thermoplastic composites.
doi:10.1016/j.jece.2026.125467: Gravity-driven membrane (GDM) filtration is a promising low-energy technology for decentralized water treatment due to its simple operation and minimal energy requirements. In this study, a series of polyamide-imide (PAI) mixed-matrix microfiltration membranes were developed by incorporating methane pyrolysis-derived pyrolytic carbon (PyC). As a low-cost by-product of methane pyrolysis, PyC offers new opportunities for resource recovery and circular carbon utilization. The PAI membrane containing 8 wt% PyC showed a humic acid feed flux of 141 LMH while maintaining excellent humic acid rejection of 99.9% during filtration of a 200 ppm humic acid solution at 5 psi and room temperature. Surface free-energy analysis indicated a lower thermodynamic tendency for humic acid adhesion after PyC incorporation, with the total adhesion free energy increasing from -2.07 mJ m -2 for the pristine PAI membrane to +1.85 mJ m -2 for the 8 wt% PyC membrane. The flux recovery ratio (FRR) increased from 59.6% for the pristine PAI membrane to 86.3% for the PyC-modified PAI membrane, demonstrating enhanced antifouling performance. PyC also improved the structural stability of the PAI matrix during the 30-6-30 °C cooling-warming cycle, with the modified membrane recovering 72% of its initial flux compared with 58% for the pristine membrane, indicating less irreversible structural change. These results indicate that PyC is a promising low-cost additive for developing GDMs with high separation performance and antifouling properties.
doi:10.1186/s40478-026-02447-z: 14-3-3 constitute a highly conserved family of proteins that participate in the regulation of essential cellular processes by establishing extensive protein-protein interactions. Consequently, perturbation of the 14-3-3s interactome can be implicated in the pathogenesis of several diseases. Phosphorylation has emerged as a key mechanism by which 14-3-3s interactome is dynamically regulated, and aberrantly phosphorylated 14-3-3s have been observed in patients with neurological disorders, among which Parkinson’s disease. Here, we investigate the role of Ser59 phosphorylation in 14-3-3γ and its impact on α-Synuclein aggregation by employing both the phosphorylated protein and the S59D phosphomimetic. Consistent with observations reported for other 14-3-3 isoforms, we found that this modification reduces the protective abilities of 14-3-3γ both in vitro and in cellular models. Importantly, this effect is also evident in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), suggesting that phosphorylation of 14-3-3γ may directly contribute to α-Synuclein aggregation in vivo and may be relevant to disease-associated mechanisms. Using bioinformatics approaches, we further examined how Ser59 phosphorylation reshapes the global 14-3-3γ interactome, revealing novel interaction networks and pathways potentially implicated in neurodegenerative disease pathogenesis.
doi:10.1002/chem.71783: ABSTRACT Excitons produced upon photoexcitation of organic semiconducting polymers (OSPs) are short lived, which limits their performance as photoactive materials. Exciton dissociation in OSPs can be enhanced by covalently conjugating them with acceptor species displaying higher electron affinity in a double cable polymer (DCP) arrangement, where non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) are emerging as attractive alternatives. Herein, we report a new all‐organic DCP comprising an electron donor polythiophene (PTh) covalently conjugated to an indoloquinoxaline (IQx) NFA (PTh‐IQx‐DCP). The selection of PTh and IQx as donor–acceptor pair is supported by the experimentally and theoretically determined favorable alignment of their band gaps and energies of HOMOs/LUMOs. The fluorescence and TRPL profiles reveal enhanced donor‐acceptor electronic communication in PTh‐IQx‐DCP. PTh‐IQx‐DCP exhibits superior photoelectrochemical characteristics compared to P3HT, IQx, and P3HT+IQx physical hybrid (PH). As photocatalyst, PTh‐IQx‐DCP produces 906 ± 38 µM.mg −1 H 2 O 2 cumulated over 10 photocatalytic cycles with a 10‐cycles apparent average turnover frequency (TOF) of 3.5 h −1 and an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 0.8% at 440 nm. The H 2 O 2 production for PTh‐IQx‐DCP averaged over 10 photocatalytic cycles is 1.6, 3.4, and 1.4 times superior compared to P3HT, IQx, and P3HT+IQx PH, respectively. Overall, this work expands the molecular design space of DCPs based photoactive materials.
doi:10.1016/j.apsusc.2026.168588: The rise of 2D semiconductors for device applications highlights the importance of band engineering. In many transition metal dichalcogenides, such as the canonical example of MoS 2 , the semiconductor band gap depends on layer number, transitioning from indirect to direct as the material thins from bulk to monolayer. Interestingly, it was predicted and experimentally confirmed that, thinning from bulk to bilayer also induces a strong blue-shift in the indirect transition. Here, we report scanning tunneling spectroscopy measurements on MoS 2 grown in situ via molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) on graphene on Ir(111) with layer thicknesses ranging from 1 to 5 layers. Our results reveal a high defect density, promoting a Stranski–Krastanov-like growth mode and defect burial in multilayer samples. We observe a drastic decrease in band gap with increasing layer number, with values even lower than that in bulk MoS 2 . Comparison with density functional theory and GW calculations suggests that the growth conditions introduce additional screening. The observed defect-induced band gap renormalization, describable by a screening potential, increases with film thickness, consistent with the rise in film disorder. Consequently, the MoS 2 multilayer system exhibits substantial lateral variation in band gap, enabling the possibility of thickness-defined lateral homojunctions.
doi:10.1038/s41529-026-00888-4: Abstract Graphene oxide-silver nanoparticles (GO-AgNPs) is a promising hybrid material for development of composites, sensors, catalysts, and antimicrobial systems. However, its degradation and life cycle remain poorly understood. Here, the chemical degradation of GO-AgNPs was investigated by sodium hypochlorite (bleach water) linked to its antimicrobial and ecotoxicological effects. This oxidative degradation was monitored up to 10 days at room temperature, revealing a progressive transformation of both components of the hybrid material. The process led to the formation of structural defects and holes in GO flakes, alongside the oxidation of AgNPs’ surfaces. These changes significantly reduce colloidal stability, leading to particle aggregation even in ultrapure water. Antimicrobial activity of GO-AgNPs before degradation showed exceptional activity but lost efficacy after the degradation. In addition, the degradation mitigated the acute toxicity to Daphnia similis but altered the feeding behavior of this aquatic model organism. Overall, this study provides crucial insights into GO-AgNPs material degradation, contributing to life cycle thinking and safe-and-sustainable by design approaches in nanotechnology and advanced materials.
doi:10.1016/j.colsurfa.2026.142043: In this study we investigated amyloid hydrogels produced by a decapeptide fragment of the acyl carrier protein (ACP) in water, in the presence of different counterions: trifluoroacetate (TFA − ), SO 4 2− , Cl − , Br − , and I − , through confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), attenuated total reflectance Fourier‑transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), circular dichroism (CD), fluorescence spectroscopy, rheological measurements, to understand how the nature of the counterion affects amyloid morphology across length scales, secondary structure, and the mechanical response of the gels. The results show that the nature of the counterion profoundly affects the gelation properties, amyloid morphology, and rheological properties. The results bear an important implication on the choice of post-synthesis counterion to accommodate a correct modeling of the system of interest.
doi:10.1002/adma.75272: ABSTRACT Polymorphism in transition‐metal dichalcogenides is typically defined based on the post‐growth phase (1T or 2H) or stabilized heterophase structures. Transient 1T‐to‐2H phase evolution is demonstrated during epitaxial growth of MoS 2 and WSe 2 on sapphire by metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD). In both systems, x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows that metallic 1T character is prominent during early stages of growth when the film is comprised of small domains and declines as domains enlarge and coalesce and the films approach stoichiometric composition. At low coverage, the XPS‐derived ex situ 1T fractions reach ≈40% of detected Mo and ≈48% of detected W and approach zero upon coalescence in both systems. Local structural observations and complementary optoelectronic evidence further corroborate the WSe 2 assignment. MoS 2 ‐specific ReaxFF molecular‐dynamics simulations indicate that small domain size and chalcogen‐deficient edge environments reduce the energetic penalty for 1T‐like formation within the model, while chalcogen vacancies facilitate local rearrangement. For WSe 2 , a multivariable growth regime with a smaller early‐stage 1T fraction also produces a substantially narrower final ensemble Φ‐scan width, motivating a possible path‐dependent influence on epitaxial development.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11005037/v1: Abstract Neural interfaces require efficient electrical coupling between living neurons and artificial devices, yet conventional electrode architectures provide limited control over the physical organization of the neuron–electrode interface. Here we report morphology-programmable organic microelectrodes formed by the controlled electrodeposition of conducting-polymer fibers directly on microelectrode arrays. By tuning the deposition conditions, we generate hierarchical dendrite-inspired architectures with controllable branching and electrochemical properties. The resulting interfaces promote nanoscale membrane conformability, reduce the neuron–electrode cleft and induce localized membrane wrapping around individual electrode branches. Short-fiber electrodes are associated with increased firing and burst rates in mature primary cortical networks, whereas longer architectures reveal position-dependent coupling along individual branches. The electrodes further support localized laser-assisted optoporation, enabling transient intracellular-like electrophysiological access while retaining extracellular recording capability. These results establish electrode morphology as a programmable design parameter for controlling the structural and electrical coupling between organic electronic devices and neuronal networks.
doi:10.3390/s26196321: This study aims to clarify how Ti and Cu doping differently influence the structural, morphological, electrical, and UV photodetection properties of Zn2SnO4 films prepared by spray pyrolysis. The comparison is based on the different chemical and electronic characteristics of the dopants and their resulting effects on charge transport and photoresponse. Zn2SnO4 films doped with 1–3 vol.% Ti or Cu were deposited under identical conditions and characterized using X-ray diffraction, atomic force microscopy, electrical measurements, and transient UV photoresponse at 365 nm. The results demonstrate distinct dopant-dependent structure–property relationships. Ti doping maintains a relatively homogeneous surface morphology and results in higher sheet resistance, whereas Cu doping produces stronger concentration-dependent morphological changes and lower sheet resistance at 1–2 vol.% Cu. The different electrical characteristics are reflected in the UV photodetection performance. The 1 vol.% Ti-doped film exhibits the highest responsivity of 239 mA/W, specific detectivity of 2.73 × 1010 Jones and a recovery time (τ90) of 74 ms, while the 3 vol.% Cu-doped film achieves the highest photo-to-dark current ratio of approximately 763 and a fast recovery time (τ90) of 70 ms. These results demonstrate that Ti and Cu provide different routes for tailoring Zn2SnO4 films for UV photodetection: Ti doping favors high responsivity and detectivity, whereas Cu doping enables efficient dark current suppression and rapid photoresponse. This study therefore establishes a direct relationship between dopant-dependent material properties and UV photodetector performance.
doi:10.1167/iovs.67.12.14: Purpose: To determine whether surface-specific biophysical properties of the internal limiting membrane (ILM), measured by atomic force microscopy (AFM), are associated with optical coherence tomography (OCT)-based epiretinal membrane (ERM) stage and six-month visual outcomes. Methods: In this prospective study, ILM specimens from vitrectomy for idiopathic ERM (stages 2-4) were examined by AFM for thickness, roughness, stiffness, and adhesion on the vitreal or retinal surface. AFM parameters were related to preoperative OCT parameters, best-corrected visual acuity, surgical grade of ILM adherence, and six-month outcomes. Multivariable regression assessed correlates of visual change and final acuity. Results: We analyzed 147 eyes (80 retinal-side, 67 vitreal-side). Retinal-side roughness and stiffness exceeded vitreal-side values (both P < 0.001). Retinal-side roughness and adhesion (P < 0.001 and P = 0.008, respectively) and, less strongly, vitreal-side stiffness (P = 0.035) increased with ERM stage, whereas vitreal-side adhesion did not. Thickness did not differ by surface or stage (all P ≥ 0.116). Retinal-side roughness and adhesion correlated with preoperative severity and postoperative outcomes, whereas vitreal-side stiffness correlated mainly with severity and vitreal-side adhesion with surgical adherence. Greater retinal-side adhesion and vitreal-side stiffness were associated with smaller visual gains and worse final acuity in multivariable models (all P < 0.05). Conclusions: ILM biophysical properties showed surface-specific associations with OCT-based ERM severity and six-month visual outcomes. Retinal-side adhesion and vitreal-side stiffness remained associated with final acuity after adjustment for baseline acuity. These findings suggest that ILM surface mechanics may reflect ERM-related retinal deformation relevant to postoperative visual recovery.
doi:10.1002/pen.70759: ABSTRACT This study investigates morphological changes during the uniaxial orientation of two fluorinated polymers, ETFE and THV. Melt‐cast monolayer films were stretched at various temperatures, including those at which they were partially molten, using a custom‐built apparatus capable of real‐time measurements of true stress, true strain, and birefringence. Complementary offline techniques, including DSC, WAXS, SAXS, and AFM, were applied at different stress and strain levels to track the evolution of structural hierarchy during stretching. THV, when stretched in a partially molten state, exhibited elastomeric behavior with nearly affine deformation, as indicated by SAXS and WAXS data showing increased lamellar spacing, reduced crystallinity, and enhanced preferred orientation. Similarly, ETFE stretched in the solid state exhibited nearly affine deformation. SAXS patterns shifted from four‐ and eight‐point patterns to a two‐point pattern in the machine direction at high strains, suggesting reoriented tilted lamellae. AFM imaging and SAXS data enabled the construction of structural hierarchy models for these polymers during orientation. These insights advance potential applications for ETFE and THV as low‐ k , high‐temperature dielectrics in fields such as HEVs and aerospace.
doi:10.1002/admi.70682: ABSTRACT Achieving precise control over nanoparticle formation remains a fundamental challenge in nanofabrication, particularly for template‐mediated synthesis. Reverse micelle deposition (RMD), using diblock copolymer nanoreactors, enables the synthesis of highly uniform nanoparticles with tunable dimensions. Directly quantifying precursor loading within these nanoreactors remains challenging, as existing techniques are often indirect or chemically specific. Here, we combine PeakForce Quantitative Nanomechanics (QNM) and Quartz Crystal Microbalance with Dissipation monitoring (QCM‐D) to independently examine precursor loading of poly(styrene)‐b‐poly(2‐vinyl pyridine) (PS‐b‐P2VP) reverse micelles. Despite probing different physical responses, both techniques exhibit the same loading‐dependent evolution, reaching a common plateau at a nominal loading ratio of ∼0.6. AFM measurements of etched nanoparticles reveal a corresponding plateau in particle size, indicating that nanoparticle formation exhibits the same loading threshold. Rather than simply demonstrating that these quantities vary with precursor loading, the independent convergence of nanomechanical, mass, and nanoparticle size measurements on the same loading threshold establishes a quantitative framework for identifying operational precursor loading limits in reverse micelle nanoreactors. As it relies on generic physical responses rather than chemically specific detection, this dual‐quantification framework should be broadly transferable across templated nanoparticle synthesis, providing an experimentally accessible strategy for comparing precursor loading behaviors and optimizing synthesis conditions.
doi:10.1016/j.polymdegradstab.2026.11248: This study investigated the chemical, structural, and morphological evolution of poly(2,5-benzimidazole)/graphene oxide (ABPBI/GO) composites exposed to 4 MeV O 2 + ion irradiation at fluences from 1 × 1 0 12 to 1 × 1 0 15 ions/cm 2 . Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy indicated dose-dependent degradation, with aromatic C=C/C=N groups exhibiting the most pronounced broadening (87.82%). X-ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis indicated the predominantly amorphous nature of ABPBI/GO, with increased peak intensities upon irradiation. Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) indicated a fluence-dependent morphological transition: surface defects increased from 286 (control) to 813 features at 1 × 1 0 14 ions/cm 2 , then coalesced into ridge-like structures at the highest fluence, where the defect count dropped to 172 features. Pore analysis indicated median pore diameters remained near ∼ 0.5 μ m , with larger pores ( > 2 μ m ) emerging at higher fluences. Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) showed non-monotonic surface roughness, with root mean square (RMS) roughness increasing from 15.38 nm (control) to a maximum of 19.68 nm at 1 × 1 0 13 ions/cm 2 , then decreasing to ∼ 13.5 nm at higher fluences. The Stopping and Range of Ions in Matter (SRIM) calculations showed that electronic stopping dominates energy deposition ( S e / S n ≈ 341 ), with peak displacements per atom (DPA) ranging from 1.61 × 1 0 − 4 to 1.61 × 1 0 − 1 , providing a quantitative link between energy deposition and the observed radiation-induced degradation.
doi:10.1016/j.cscm.2026.e06603: This study aims to quantitatively analyse the morphological and micromechanical properties of asphalt binders using Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) and to investigate the sensitivity of results to changes in the testing protocol. Two asphalt binders with different penetration grades were subjected to various ageing treatments, resulting in changes in their colloidal structure. Two AFM test protocols were defined, differing in method of sample preparation and probe type. Microstructural parameters, including surface roughness, bee structure parameters (number, area, coverage, size), as well as domain areas, were obtained by means of tests carried out in the tapping mode. Additionally, parameters resulting from Force Distance Curve (FDC) tests, such as adhesion force and Derjaguin-Muller-Toporov (DMT) modulus, were calculated. Finally, experimental results were compared to synthetic indices derived from the chemical characterization of bulk asphalt binders, with the ultimate goal of identifying the AFM protocol that better reveals the inherent characteristics of the considered materials. It was found that the evolution in the number of bee structures due to ageing is highly related to the colloidal structure of asphalt binders. Furthermore, the morphology images and microstructural parameters were found to be strongly dependent upon the adopted testing protocols, with protocol 2 generally exhibiting stronger correlations between bee-structure parameters and chemical composition. Notably, the absolute correlation coefficients between bee number and the SARA indices ranged from 0.17 to 0.32 for protocol 1 and 0.71 to 0.77 for protocol 2, while those for bee size ranged from 0.69 to 0.85 and 0.96 to 0.97, respectively. Micromechanical assessment revealed that the amount of polar fractions in the asphalt binder was found to be strongly associated with adhesion force. The results also highlighted the potential need to adjust the target peak force according to the probe type and asphalt binder stiffness to ensure accurate DMT modulus measurements.
doi:10.3390/biomimetics11100713: The present study reports the development of a novel botanical hybrid system obtained through the integration of Geranium robertianum L. phytochemicals, green-synthesized silver nanoparticles, and chlorophyll-loaded soybean lecithin biomimetic membranes. The proposed strategy combines the reducing and stabilizing capacity of plant-derived metabolites with the structural and functional advantages of membrane-inspired lipid assemblies. Silver nanoparticles were synthesized using aqueous Geranium robertianum extract, while biomimetic lipid vesicles were prepared from soybean lecithin and subsequently assembled into hybrid bioentities through a self-organization process. The obtained structures were characterized by UV–Vis spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, FTIR–ATR analysis, dynamic light scattering, zeta potential measurements, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. Optical investigations support the formation of phyto-capped silver nanoparticles and their successful incorporation into chlorophyll-containing biomimetic membranes. The hybrid structures exhibited improved colloidal stability, appropriate nanoscale dimensions, and characteristic morphological features indicative of efficient integration of the lipid and metallic components. Antioxidant and antibacterial investigations highlighted the combined contribution of the phytochemicals, silver nanostructures, and phospholipid matrix. These findings establish a versatile, environmentally friendly platform that bridges phytochemistry, nanotechnology, and biomimetic engineering, and may provide new opportunities for the development of multifunctional antimicrobial systems.
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70972-x: Abstract The fabrication of cost-effective LCS\WC–Co layered composites with high mechanical reliability remains a significant challenge. In this study, bilayer composites were fabricated by powder metallurgy at a compaction pressure of 313 MPa and a sintering temperature of 1300 °C, and the effect of a Ni interlayer combined with varying Co contents was systematically investigated. Microstructural analyses showed that the LCS\Ni\WC–Co composites exhibited defect-free interfaces with minimal porosity and relative densities exceeding 93.2%, indicating strong metallurgical bonding. XRD results revealed that the Ni interlayer effectively suppressed the formation of the brittle η-phase (Fe 3 W 3 C) compared with directly bonded LCS\WC–Co composites by modifying interfacial diffusion and promoting the formation of (Ni,Co)-based solid solutions. Consequently, the Ni-containing composites exhibited improved wear resistance and lower coefficients of friction. Among the investigated compositions, LCS\Ni\WC–12Co achieved the highest performance, with a bonding strength of 240 MPa, fracture toughness of 28 MPa m 1/2 , hardness of 700 HV, and a coefficient of friction of 0.38. These findings demonstrate that Ni interlayer engineering effectively enhances interfacial stability, suppresses detrimental phase formation, and promotes a favorable balance between hardness, toughness, and tribological performance.
doi:10.1002/adfm.78793: ABSTRACT We introduce ligand‐assisted epitaxial growth (LAEG) for lead‐halide perovskites, enabling the formation of high‐quality, single‐crystalline epitaxial microstructures. In this approach, ligands fulfill multiple critical functions: they regulate crystal growth by slowing crystallization kinetics, allowing the formation of epitaxial microcrystals with smooth surfaces and well‐defined morphologies; they protect the perovskite from environmental degradation; and they passivate surface states. Near‐ambient‐pressure X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirms well‐preserved surface stoichiometry of CsPbBr 3 enabled by ligand protection. The LAEG method is broadly applicable to different ligands, perovskite compositions, and substrates, consistently yielding higher material quality than non‐ligand‐assisted solution epitaxy. CsPbBr 3 epitaxial microcrystals exhibit a high photoluminescence quantum yield of ∼50% and nearly temperature‐independent photoluminescence decay dynamics up to 80°C, demonstrating strong thermal robustness relevant for optoelectronic devices. Lasing is observed up to 90°C, and improved thermal management enhances operational lifetime. Micro‐resonator lasers grown on mica substrates exhibit record‐low threshold excitation powers among microcrystal‐based perovskite lasers, outperforming previously reported CsPbBr 3 devices and those grown on PbS substrates due to favorable refractive‐index contrast enabling total internal reflection. Overall, LAEG provides a simple yet powerful route to high‐quality perovskite epitaxy and is expected to be extendable to lower‐dimensional perovskite systems with enhanced and tunable optical properties.
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-72641-5: Abstract Saponins are amphiphilic natural compounds whose membrane activity is commonly attributed to sterol complexation, whereas their effects on sterol-free membranes remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how lipid packing governs the interaction of a Saponaria officinalis saponin extract with cholesterol-free phosphatidylcholine (PC) and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) membranes using differential scanning calorimetry, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, small-angle X-ray scattering, dynamic light scattering, atomic force microscopy, and calcein-release assays. Saponins reduced the cooperativity of lipid phase transitions and disrupted collective lipid rearrangements in all systems, but the extent of membrane reorganization was strongly lipid dependent. PC membranes showed pronounced disruption of lamellar organization, reduced assembly size, and increased structural heterogeneity, whereas PE membranes were more resistant, with short-chain PE displaying heterogeneous lamellar organization and long-chain PE showing only minor structural changes. These differences were accompanied by lipid-dependent membrane permeabilization, with substantially greater calcein release from PC than from PE liposomes. Overall, saponins can reorganize sterol-free membranes through mechanisms governed by lipid packing and interfacial interactions. Saponins therefore affect membrane barrier function even without cholesterol, with phospholipid composition determining the magnitude and nature of the response.
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78460-6: Abstract Double-strand break repair (DSBR) is essential for genome integrity, yet mechanistic details of error-prone microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) remain unclear. A bacterial group II intron-like reverse transcriptase, G2L4 RT, has been implicated in MMEJ, but how it executes DSBR is unknown. Using high-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM), we directly visualize G2L4 RT-mediated DSBR via MMEJ. We observe that G2L4 RT dimers exhibit RT3a plug protrusion upon DNA engagement and catalyze MMEJ by binding and stabilizing a 4-bp annealed microhomology and filling adjacent single-strand gaps with dNTPs. We also observe Mn 2+ -stimulated terminal transferase activity that generates elongated and branched DNA intermediates prior to ligation. With T4 DNA ligase, we visualize binding near nick sites and real-time nick sealing, which stabilizes the repaired products and suppresses off-pathway branching. These results reveal how G2L4 RT and ligase activities shape MMEJ intermediates and outcomes.
doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15009871/v1: Anion exchange doping (AED) is a key strategy for optimizing organic thermoelectrics (OTEs).However, the influence of specific polymer microstructures like polymorphs on AED has received relatively little attention.Here, we investigate the interplay between thermally induced polymorphism in poly(dodecyl-quaterthiophene) (PQT) and sequential AED efficiency using FeCl3 and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI).By precisely fabricating microstructural gradients via a custom thermal annealing stage, we rapidly screen AED behavior across a spectrum of structural states within a single PQT film.We reveal that pre-set polymorphism acts as a fundamental gating mechanism for dopant infiltration.The expanded lamellar spacing of the (100) polymorph, formed after annealing at elevated temperatures, allows for greater dopant uptake, and thus enables electronic conductivity () as high as 522.0 ± 23.0 S/cm and a maximum power factor of 15.4 μW/mK 2 .Conversely, the tighter (100)' polymorph restricts doping level and structural ordering.This work establishes that pre-forming the (100) polymorph is a critical prerequisite for maximizing charge transport and thermoelectric performance in sequentially doped PQT.
doi:10.1186/s12964-026-03282-4: Abstract Background Synucleinopathies are a group of neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the misfolding, aggregation, and accumulation of α-synuclein (α-syn) into oligomeric assemblies and amyloid inclusions. Alongside neurons, glial cells can internalize pathological α-syn and play a major role in its degradation.
