Given that microRNAs (miRNAs) modulate endocytic pathways and multiple aspects of α-syn biology, we performed an unbiased genome-wide microRNA mimic screen to identify miRNAs that influence α-syn fibril uptake. Methods An image-based high-throughput screen of arrayed miRNAs was conducted in the U-87 MG glioblastoma cell line. Differential fluorescent and immunolabeling distinguished intracellular from extracellular α-syn PFFs, enabling quantification of miRNA-dependent effects on α-syn uptake. The lead miRNA identified in the primary screen was subsequently validated by flow cytometry in three glioblastoma cell lines and in mature hiPSC-derived astrocytes, using fluorescently labeled α-syn PFFs, monomeric α-syn, Tau-K18 fibrils, and PD-, DLB-, and MSA-seeded α-syn fibrils. Results In our primary screen, we identified nine enhancers and eight suppressors of α-syn preformed fibril (PFF) internalization. Orthogonal validation revealed miR-517a-3p as a robust suppressor of uptake, reducing PFF internalization by ~ 73% at early time points, with significant reductions maintained after 48 and 72 h of fibril exposure. miR-517a-3p did not accelerate degradation or secretion of internalized fibrils, indicating that it primarily impairs uptake rather than downstream processing. It also decreased internalization of monomeric α-syn and Tau-K18 fibrils, as well as PD-, DLB-, and MSA-seeded α-syn fibrils, while increasing transferrin uptake, indicating a cargo-selective rather than global effect on endocytosis. The inhibitory effect was reproduced in two additional glioblastoma lines (U-251 MG, LN-229). The effect extended to mature hiPSC-derived astrocytes, where miR-517a-3p reduced α-syn PFF uptake relative to the vehicle-treated control, although not below the untransfected baseline. Conclusions Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role of miRNAs in the regulation of pathogenic protein aggregate internalization, suggesting that miRNA-dependent control of endocytosis…
doi:10.1016/j.fpp.2026.100139: ABSTRACT The selective ablation behaviour of nanocomposite thin films under femtosecond laser irradiation was systematically investigated. The experimental sample, a Nb/Ti multilayer nanocomposite consisting of alternating metallic bilayers deposited on a Si substrate, was fabricated by ion sputtering. The fluence range for selective photomechanical ablation, e.g. the selective removal of nano-layers, is determined and spatial periodicity of laser induced periodic surface structures was estimated for the given experimental conditions. Single-pulse laser irradiation was carried out in air using a focused, linearly polarized Gaussian beam with pulse duration of 170 fs and a wavelength of 513 nm. To induce selective removal of one or two individual nano-layers within the multilayer thin film, the laser fluence was varied from 0.05 to 1.0 J/cm². Detailed morphological analysis of the irradiated spots revealed well-defined selective ablation of the top one or two layers, depending on the applied fluence. Furthermore, multi-pulse irradiation with up to 20 overlapping pulses resulted in the formation of periodic surface structures on the Nb/Ti nano-layer thin film, which can be attributed to interference between the incident laser field and surface-scattered waves on roughness formed after the first laser pulse.
doi:10.1002/nap2.70300: ABSTRACT The integration of membranes into optical resonators plays a key role in a variety of applications, including optomechanics. Membranes hosting single photon emitters, ideally with access to spin states, open new roads toward (spin‐) optomechanics. Hexagonal boron nitride is among the most promising two‐dimensional materials showing excellent optical and mechanical properties combined with the ability to host optical active (spin‐) defects. The deterministic creation of optically active defect centers in hexagonal boron nitride membranes and their coupling to optomechanical systems is an outstanding challenge. Here, we explore an alternative, hybrid approach in order to establish coupling between a single photon emitter in commercially available hexagonal boron nitride flakes and a fiber‐cavity mode. We solve technical challenges, such as scattering losses arising from an uncontrolled flake topography. We extend our work by positioning the single photon emitter in hexagonal boron nitride flakes on a highly strained silicon nitride membrane in a membrane‐in‐the‐middle configuration. The mechanical vibrational modes of the silicon nitride membrane and cavity‐coupled emission from the single photon emitter are simultaneously observed. Our work is a first step toward the realization of a cavity optomechanics platform with an incorporated single photon emitter.
doi:10.1016/j.jcis.2026.141703: Hypothesis Self-cleaning and antifouling coatings based on superhydrophilic surfaces offer potential advantages respect superhydrophobic, being effective against non-polar and polar contaminants. Their reported action mechanism involves the formation of a water layer that decreases interaction with contaminants, though this does not consider the cleaning in dry conditions. Adhesion to the surface is largely dependent on the interfacial interactions between all phases involved (surface-contaminant-cleaning media). Hence, a comprehensive analysis of interfacial tensions should be able to predict the self-cleaning performance on different scenarios. Experiments A theoretical approach was proposed to estimate the work of adhesion and its variation respect the coating surface energy components for different contaminants-cleaning configurations: (i) polar powder removal by water; (ii) soot removal with air; (iii) Oil-contaminated powder removal by water and (iv) bacterial adhesion. The methodology is based on the balance of interfacial tensions in the surface-contaminant-media system, using Owens-Wendt-Rabel-Kaelble and Good's models. A TiO 2 –ormosil coating, combining photoactivated superhydrophilic surface with hydrophobicity inside the pores was applied on cement mortar for experimental validation. Superhydrophobic surfaces and hydrophobic surfaces (w/o TiO 2 ) were also evaluated to discern the effects of roughness. Findings The calculations correctly predicted a markedly lower adhesion of the non-polar and biological contaminants to the superhydrophilic surfaces, as confirmed by the experimental results. In addition, we prove and explain for the first time the removal of soot in dry conditions. A satisfactory performance was confirmed on polar contaminants, explained by the similar calculated adhesion respect the superhydrophobic surface and decreased water absorption and micro-roughness.
doi:10.1021/acsnano.6c07014: Transition metal ditellurides exhibit structural and electronic properties distinct from their selenide and sulfide counterparts, including the stabilization of multiple charge density wave (CDW) phases. Within the niobium compound family, notable differences in structure are also observed: bulk NbTe2 crystallizes in the 1T phase, distinguishing it from NbSe2 and NbS2, which typically adopt both the 2H and 1T structures. However, in this work, we report the unexpectedly successful synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) islands of the metastable 1H-NbTe2 phase via molecular beam epitaxy on epitaxial graphene supported on Ir(111). The phase is identified by its characteristic hexagonal lattice in combination with distinct spectroscopic features and the presence of mirror twin boundaries. A comprehensive analysis combining scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirms the metallic character and structural stability of the 1H-NbTe2 phase. Furthermore, low-temperature STS measurements reveal the formation of a 4 × 4 CDW modulation, which is explained based on a phonon instability. These findings motivate the exploration of the complex phase behavior and electronic properties of NbTe2 in the 2D limit.
doi:10.1021/acsomega.6c04722: Abstract Arranging colloidal particles on surfaces with tunable interparticle distances, like in non-close-packed structures (NCPS), is important for many applications. However, controlling their formation remains challenging. Although particle and substrate roughness, along with electrostatic repulsion, affect colloidal interactions, their combined effect on colloidal arrangement remains poorly understood. Therefore, model silica particles with smooth, medium-rough, and rough, virus-like morphologies were synthesized. Virus-like particle synthesis was optimized for controlled roughness (Rq = 1.4–5.1 nm) and low polydispersity (∼5%). Amine-functionalized particles dispersed in water and aqueous LaCl3 solutions were transferred onto gold substrates of two different roughnesses to form NCPS. Only the two roughest particle types (Rq = 4.3 and 5.0 nm) formed three-dimensional aggregates on rough substrates, likely due to pre-aggregation in dispersion, which could be driven by roughness-mediated mechanical interlocking. By varying ionic strength, the effect of electrostatic repulsion on interparticle distances of differently rough particles (Rq = 0.3–2.1 nm) is investigated. The rougher the particles, the less an increasing ionic strength reduces interparticle distances. At low ionic strengths, interparticle distances of rough particles (Rq = 2.1 nm) are independent of ionic strength. Smoother substrates promote lateral mobility for all particles, reducing interparticle distances more strongly for smooth particles. However, aggregation of particles with Rq = 2.1 nm remains almost the same on both substrates (Rq = 0.57 and 1.62 nm), while it increases significantly for smoother particles, suggesting that roughness-induced frictional forces are more important at short distances. These findings reveal that adjusting surface roughness can facilitate controlled particle arrangements.
doi:10.1016/j.carbpol.2026.125911: The isolation of cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs), a promising precursor for sustainable and high-performance materials, has relied on chemically intensive, energy-demanding processes. As these processes were originally designed for the isolation of CNFs from wood, we herein show that the intrinsic ultrastructure of non-structural plant cells provides unique opportunities, namely direct access to loosely organized cellulose nanonetworks. We demonstrate that this loose nanofibrillar tissue can be transformed into CNFs with sizes down to elementary nanofibrils (~4 nm) at high yields (reaching ~32%) under exceptionally mild hydrothermal conditions. Three distinct plants were evaluated and the physicochemical properties of the obtained nanonetworks and corresponding CNFs were thoroughly studied, including the hydrodynamics of the resulting gels. Films prepared from the obtained CNFs showed similar performance to those obtained from conventionally isolated wood-based CNFs. Overall, this study demonstrates that CNFs can be obtained through minimal processes from widely available biomass. Thus, this approach offers a unique shift in the range of opportunities for the production of CNFs, facilitating the integration of their use into the food supply chain, biomedical applications, and other regulatory-constrained applications.
doi:10.1016/j.jclepro.2026.149574: Dry microbial biostimulants offer a convenient and sustainable approach to enhancing crop health and yield. However, their efficacy is limited by the challenge of stabilizing microbes into dry products because scalable dehydration methods such as spray drying impose substantial thermal and osmotic stresses that often result in substantial viability losses. In this work, metal-phenolic network (MPN) coatings were applied to Klebsiella michiganensis M5al, a Gram-negative, plant-beneficial bacteria, prior to spray drying to enable their survival during the rapid thermal dehydration process. Uncoated cells lost 5.0 ± 0.21 log viability during spray drying, whereas tannic-acid-iron coatings reduced this loss to 3.2 ± 0.34 log with a streamlined, single-coat process, and 2.1 ± 0.47 log with a two-coat process. Furthermore, phenolics present in water extracts of spent coffee grounds (SCG) were shown to form MPNs with protective performance comparable to those formed from purified tannic acid, reducing viability loss during spray drying to 3.5 ± 0.19 log. Nano-scale infrared spectroscopy confirmed the presence of metal-phenolic coatings on cell surfaces, while atomic force microscopy indicated improved structural preservation during spray-drying. These findings show that SCG-derived phenolics can serve as sustainable feedstocks for protective MPN coatings and demonstrate the feasibility of using waste-derived phenolics as functional substitutes for purified reagents in MPN coatings. This approach simultaneously enables scalable production of dry microbial biostimulants and valorization of abundant, phenolic-rich agro-industrial residues.
doi:10.1016/j.mfglet.2026.08.076: This study investigated the effect of electrical discharge machining parameters, gap voltage, peak current, and pulse-on time on material removal rate, electrode wear rate, and surface roughness during the machining of nickel-based Hastelloy C-276. Copper was selected as the electrode material for all experiments. The experimental trials were designed according to a face-centered composite design within the response surface methodology framework. The significance of each process variable was determined through Analysis of Variance. Optimization of machining responses was achieved using the desirability function approach. Validation experiments conducted under these optimized conditions yielded relative errors of 5.6 % for material removal rate, 4.2 % for electrode wear rate, and 7.6 % for surface roughness. The analysis revealed that peak current has the most dominant effect on the machining characteristics among the investigated parameters. Despite electrical discharge machining being highly effective for machining hard materials by means of controlled electrical discharges, it often results in surface defects such as micro-cracks, recast layers, and reduced surface integrity. Therefore, the comparative study has also been performed in terms of surface characteristics of electrical discharge machining and grinding-produced parts at optimized input parameters. In the results section, the grinding-produced surface outpaces the electrical discharge machining surface in context with surface characteristics. Furthermore, a sustainability assessment using the process sustainability index indicates that grinding with Jatropha-based green fluid offers a more environmentally and socially responsible alternative to electrical discharge machining, achieving a higher overall sustainability score. Other than parameter optimization, the present work compares the EDM and grinding processes in terms of surface characteristics and sustainability performance. The central objective of the work is to evaluate the machining efficiency and sustainability considerations for Hastelloy C-276. © 2026 The Authors. Published by ELSEVIER Ltd. doi:10.1097/gox.0000000000008090: Background: Poly-d,l-lactic acid (PDLLA) and calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) are injectable biostimulators increasingly used as skin boosters. Although both promote tissue regeneration, their comparative histological effects in humans remain poorly characterized, particularly regarding differential vascular, collagenous, and elastinrelated responses that may influence individualized treatment strategies and clinical decision-making. Methods: This institutional review board-approved prospective split-face pilot study included 3 female patients (6 cheeks) who received PDLLA injection on one side and CaHA injection on the contralateral side. Biopsies were obtained 3 months after injection from corresponding preauricular or temporal facial regions during the facelift procedure for histological and immunohistochemical evaluation, including hematoxylin and eosin, Herovici, Verhoeff-Van Gieson, and CD31/CD34 immunostaining. Ultrasound (33 MHz) and surface roughness analysis were also performed, alongside Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale scoring. Results: Both PDLLA and CaHA demonstrated regenerative activity, though their predominant effects differed. PDLLA was associated with greater angiogenesis (capillary counts and CD31 staining), fibroblast activation, and early collagen remodeling. CaHA exhibited higher elastin fiber density (13% increase by Verhoeff-Van Gieson staining), stronger CD34 expression, and more pronounced early dermal thickening on ultrasound. Both agents improved clinical skin roughness and Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale scores without major adverse events. Conclusions: PDLLA and CaHA skin boosters each demonstrated distinct yet beneficial biostimulatory profiles in human tissue. PDLLA favored angiogenesis and collagen remodeling, whereas CaHA promoted elastogenesis, progenitor cell activation, and early tissue reinforcement. These findings highlight the complementary roles of PDLLA and CaHA and underscore the need for larger, long-term studies to refine their clinical applications.
doi:10.1002/adpr.70293: The photothermal response of a gold nanorods array to near‐infrared irradiation is used to dynamically tune the Bragg reflection band of adjacent cholesteric liquid crystal (CLC) layers. By cascading two CLC cells with opposite handedness (right‐ and left‐handed) and with the same peak Bragg wavelength, a compact device capable of reflecting nearly 100% of unpolarized incident light is achieved. The thermoplasmonic heating enables reversible spectral tuning of the reflection band over ~80 nm in the visible range via temperature‐induced changes in birefringence and pitch. This strategy demonstrates a remotely actuated and contact‐free platform for tunable optical filters, with potential applications in smart photonic devices, optical communications, sensing, and liquid crystal displays.
doi:10.1002/adom.71937: ABSTRACT Hybrid organic‐inorganic halide perovskites are attractive semiconductors for optoelectronics, but their electrical and photoresponse are often affected by slow ion‐mediated processes. Although ion migration and history‐dependent photoresponse are well established in halide perovskites, how these mixed ionic‐electronic effects depend on device architecture remains unclear. Here, we investigate solution‐grown MAPbBr 3 microwires integrated onto interdigitated Au electrodes in two representative configurations: a single‐gap (SG) device and a multi‐gap (MG) device comprising five parallel electrically active regions. Combining dark and illuminated current‐voltage measurements, SCLC analysis, and time‐resolved photocurrent measurements under pulsed broadband illumination, we reveal markedly different hysteretic and transient behaviors in the two contact configurations. The SG device exhibits pronounced illumination‐history‐dependent transients and strongly power‐dependent transport, consistent with a significant contribution from local ionic polarization, trap‐mediated processes, and contact injection. In contrast, the MG device displays a more stable and weakly power‐dependent photoresponse. A phenomenological parallel‐channel model shows that the measured polarization‐induced voltage offset in a multi‐gap architecture can be expressed as a conductance‐weighted contribution of the local polarization potentials associated with the individual electrically active regions. These results provide an architecture‐dependent framework for understanding how contact configuration modulates mixed ionic–electronic transport and hysteresis in MAPbBr3 microwire devices.
doi:10.1002/pat.70776: ABSTRACT In this article, regenerated silk fibroin (SF) films were modified using atmospheric‐pressure dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma to enhance their physicochemical, structural, and mechanical properties for potential biomedical applications. Plasma treatment was performed using an argon–oxygen gas mixture under optimized operating conditions. The plasma‐induced modifications were systematically characterized by water contact angle measurements, attenuated total reflectance Fourier‐transform infrared (ATR–FTIR) spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy (SEM–EDS), x‐ray diffraction (XRD), and uniaxial tensile testing. Plasma treatment markedly increased the surface wettability, reducing the water contact angle from approximately 80° to 20°. Quantitative AFM analysis revealed a decrease in the mean surface roughness (Ra) from 9.64 to 7.32 nm, indicating a measurable change in nanoscale surface topography under the selected treatment conditions. ATR–FTIR analysis revealed subtle changes in the surface chemical environment while preserving the characteristic molecular structure of silk fibroin. XRD analysis demonstrated an increase in crystallinity from 37.3% to 46.3%, indicating improved molecular ordering of the existing crystalline domains without the formation of new crystalline phases. These structural changes were accompanied by enhanced mechanical performance, with Young's modulus increasing from 3.30 to 4.20 GPa and tensile strength from 53.46 to 70.59 MPa, while the elongation at break remained essentially unchanged. The combined results demonstrate that atmospheric‐pressure DBD plasma provides an effective, environmentally friendly, and solvent‐free post‐treatment strategy for engineering the physicochemical, structural, and mechanical properties of RSF films without compromising their structural integrity. The simultaneous improvement in surface hydrophilicity, molecular organization, and mechanical performance highlights the potential of plasma‐treated silk fibroin films for advanced biomedical applications, including tissue engineering, wound healing, and implantable biomaterials.
doi:10.1098/rsos.260025: Abstract Interpenetrating polymer networks (IPNs) consist of two or more cross-linked polymers that are intertwined and cannot be separated, providing excellent stability and strong integration of the components. In this study, hydrophilic and semicrystalline poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) was blended with hydrophobic and amorphous 1,3-polybutadiene (PBu) to form an amphiphilic material with enhanced mechanical and thermal properties. This blending reduced PEO crystallinity and promoted phase separation while enabling tailored surface interactions, which is advantageous for coatings requiring strong adhesion to both polar and non-polar substrates. The addition of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) further improved the thermal stability, mechanical performance, processing behaviour and crystallinity of the PEO–PBu blend. To achieve permanent structural integration, electrospun PEO–PBu–CNT nanofibres were subjected to UV-initiated cross-linking with pentaerythritol triacrylate (PETA), introducing additional covalent bonds between the polymer chains. Cross-linking reduced the flexibility and vibrational freedom of C─H bonds, as indicated by decreased Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR)spectroscopy peak intensity. Overall, the synergistic effects of amphiphilic blending, CNT incorporation and UV-induced cross-linking yielded IPNs with optimized crystallinity, enhanced robustness and improved interfacial interactions. These findings highlight the promise of PEO–PBu–CNT IPNs for advanced functional materials for applications, such as solid polymer electrolytes and sensors, where mechanical durability, thermal stability and controlled ionic transport are essential.
doi:10.1088/1748-605x/aeae94: Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM)-based hydrogels in previous research demonstrated as promising biomimetic scaffolds. However, conventional decellularization protocols are commonly based on harsh detergents that disrupt extracellular matrix (ECM) integrity. While milder detergents such as sodium lauryl ether sulfate (SLES) and physical methods like ultrasonication have been proposed to reduce these negative effects, their combined application and the influence of ultrasonication parameters remain insufficiently explored. In this study, we systematically investigated the effect of ultrasonication-assisted decellularization on porcine liver tissue treated with SLES, with particular emphasis on ultrasonication exposure time. Decellularization efficiency and ECM preservation were evaluated through DNA, collagen, and glycosaminoglycan quantification, and structural integrity analysis. The impact of processing conditions on downstream applications was assessed by characterizing the gelation behavior, rheological properties, molecular weight distribution, and microstructure of the resulting dECM-based hydrogels. Biocompatibility was evaluated using HaCaT cells through metabolic assay and adhesion. Ultrasonication-assisted decellularization improved ECM preservation while maintaining effective decellularization, as all samples had < 50 ng of DNA per mg of dry tissue. Furthermore, it enabled the formation of hydrogels with enhanced physicochemical properties and increased cell viability compared to hydrogels obtained by detergent decellularization only. These findings demonstrate that controlled ultrasonication can reduce the need for harsh chemical treatments and improve scaffold preservation, highlighting its potential for optimizing decellularization protocols in tissue engineering applications.
doi:10.3390/plants15193014: Urban vineyards are expanding worldwide, driven by cultural and environmental motivations and their potential contribution to sustainable food systems. This study assessed grapevine (Vitis vinifera L.) responses to urban atmospheric conditions and explored traits relevant to cultivar selection and particulate matter (PM) interception. Research was conducted during the 2025 growing season in a highly biodiverse urban vineyard comprising 170 cultivars at the Botanical Garden of Rome (Italy), a city where grapevine has been documented since antiquity. Digital phenotyping was used to screen 54 cultivars based on leaf micromorphological traits, followed by detailed assessment of five selected cultivars. Measurements also included leaf anatomical traits, chlorophyll content, spectral reflectance-derived indices related to vigor and water status, and PM interception by scanning electron microscopy. Cultivars differed in micromorphological traits and ecophysiological proxies, suggesting different responses to urban environmental conditions. Total leaf-surface PM accumulation after an approximately 20-day accumulation period following the last intense rainfall event (>10 mm h−1) ranged from 52,024 particles mm−2 in cv. Barbera to 77,462 particles mm−2 in cv. Maturano, values broadly comparable to those reported for some urban forest species. Deposition on the adaxial surface was more than twice that measured on the abaxial surface. These findings highlight the potential of digital phenotyping to integrate morphological and physiological traits, supporting plant material selection for urban viticulture, PM interception, and, more broadly, for urban landscape design.
doi:10.18323/2782-4039-2026-3-77-2: Problem. For W–Co coatings on low-carbon structural steel, the influence of the combined variation of the discrete MODE and VIBRATION parameters during electrospark alloying on layer formation and the coordinated change in its structural and tribological characteristics has not been established. This complicates the selection of a mode that simultaneously provides coating density, strong adhesion to the substrate, and wear resistance. Aim. To identify the influence of electrospark alloying modes with W–Co electrodes on the structure and tribological properties of coatings on St3 steel. Methods. Coatings were deposited onto St3 steel specimens measuring 50×50×3 mm using electrodes composed of 85 % W and 15 % Co, produced by spark plasma sintering. On a UR-121 setup, five MODE and VIBRATION combinations were investigated with five passes and a processing time of 180 s. The structure and properties were evaluated using SEM, X-ray phase analysis, 3D profilometry, measurements of microhardness, porosity, and adhesion; tribological tests were carried out according to the ball-on-flat scheme. Results. Among the five studied modes, the optimal combination was MODE=2, VIBRATION=5, which formed the densest layer about 75 μm thick with a microhardness of 1520±45 HV, porosity not exceeding 1.5 %, and adhesion of 75 MPa. The α-Fe, W, Co, Fe–W, WO3, and WC phases were identified. At a load of 1 N, the mass wear intensity was 0.04–0.08 mg/(N·m), which is 2.5–4 times lower than that of uncoated St3 steel (0.15–0.20 mg/(N·m). Conclusions. The MODE=2, VIBRATION=5 mode provides the best combination of microhardness, low porosity, adhesion, and wear resistance among those studied and can be used as a basis for local restoration of worn surfaces of agricultural machinery parts.
doi:10.1016/j.apsusc.2026.168538: Copper–silver (CuAg) alloys are increasingly explored for applications in high-performance electrical and electronic systems, owing to their unique combination of high electrical and thermal conductivity and enhanced mechanical strength. Nevertheless, a thorough understanding of how these alloys surface characteristics influence properties remains largely underdeveloped. Here, we explored the complex interplay between surface texture morphology, layer composition, wetting, and optical properties of Cu, Ag, and CuAg thin films deposited on textured silicon substrates via magnetron sputtering. Employing data mining and machine learning techniques, we identified correlations between contact angle and surface fractal dimension across all layer types promoting Cassie-Baxter surface state formation. Our analysis revealed a connection between layer thickness and surface topography entropy deficit, suggesting a dynamic evolution of surface order/disorder during metal film growth. Furthermore, we observed that contact angle sensitivity to layer thickness implied correlation with microstructure evolution. Through K-Means clustering, we successfully categorized the formed surface textures morphology. Finally, a Random Forest regression model was developed to predict water contact angles (Mean Absolute Error around 5 deg) using only texture and optical parameters. The model, along with Python code, is publicly available. Our findings establish pathway towards targeted surface texture morphology engineering for tailored material performance.
doi:10.1021/acs.langmuir.6c01280: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) and solvent composition critically influence the orientation and electronic properties of functional organic molecules, paving the way for energy conversion and optoelectronic devices. PeakForce quantitative nanomechanics atomic force microscopy (AFM) was used to investigate pyrene-based 2H-pyran[7]helicene (P,S,S)-(+) and its mirror image, 2H-pyran[7]helicene (M,R,R)-(-), deposited on self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) with one of the following headgroups: adamantyl, phenyl, and trityl. By varying toluene content and dilution during spin-coating, we achieve changes to the topography, mechanical properties, and work function of our surfaces and are able to link these changes to the achievement of limited control over the modulation of the helicene orientation and gain insight into the self-assembly process on said SAMs. At high dilutions, we were able to detect distinct nucleation sites for helicene structures. These orientational changes and associated disorder correlate directly with work function modulation, suggesting a way and a mechanism for tuning electronic properties via these interfaces. Our findings hint at a simple processing strategy to engineer the molecular orientation and work function, advancing the design of helicene-based optoelectronic materials.
doi:10.1021/acsomega.6c07322: Abstract The design of transparent top electrodes is essential for the implementation of advanced photovoltaic technologies, such as building-integrated photovoltaics, agrovoltaics, and tandem devices. In this context, perovskite solar cells implemented with transparent electrodes can emerge as a leading technology due to their tunable optical bandgap and high power conversion efficiency. However, achieving high transparency remains a critical bottleneck, as top electrodes are typically based on opaque noble metal films. This creates an inherent trade-off between electrical conductivity and optical transparency, which limits the overall device performance. In this work, Au-based dielectric/metal/dielectric (D/M/D) multilayers were systematically investigated as top electrodes in both chemically symmetric and asymmetric configurations, employing MoOx and WOx as dielectric layers. Through a multitechnique characterization approach, it was demonstrated that the careful design of the selected materials and thicknesses of the Au-based D/M/D constituting layers enables precise tuning of their optical properties. In particular, changing from symmetric to asymmetric configurations provides additional degrees of freedom for light management, enabling the independent modulation of transmittance in the visible and near-infrared spectral regions. The symmetric stacks tend to maximize transmittance in both regions simultaneously, and the asymmetric design allows for selective optimization of transparency in the different spectral ranges. The optimized D/M/D electrodes maintain a low sheet resistance of 4.2 Ω/sq, while reaching transmittance maxima higher than 75%, significantly surpassing standard metallic electrodes. The Au-based D/M/D multilayers herein implemented were successfully integrated as a hole-collecting top electrode into n–i–p semitransparent perovskite solar cells, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13%, comparable to reference devices, but providing significantly enhanced and modulable optical transparency. This strategy establishes Au-based D/M/D architectures as versatile multilayers for next-generation photovoltaics with finely tunable spectrally selective properties.
doi:10.1002/star.70303: ABSTRACT Unripe banana cultivars are being utilized to produce starchy flours with diverse applications. The primary component of these flours is starch, and understanding its multi‐scale structure is crucial for determining their functional, physicochemical, and digestibility properties. This study examines the multi‐scale structure of starch from two cooking hybrid (AAB) and two dessert pure (AAA) banana cultivars. Particle size distribution, x‐ray diffraction, and light, scanning electron, and atomic force microscopies revealed distinctive morphological, molecular, and thermal features. Notably, hybrid cultivars displayed elongated granules with increased fluorescence and higher gelatinization temperatures. These findings suggest that the genotype of banana cultivars significantly influences the structure and properties of their starch, and understanding these differences can inform the selection of cultivars for specific end‐uses.
doi:10.1002/adem.71286: Friction‐induced recycling is a method to recycle aluminum with a lower energy footprint than conventional methods. However, the quality of a metal–metal joint is strongly influenced by surface contamination, in particular by naturally formed oxide layers. Octadecyl phosphonic acid and methyl diphosphonic acid self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are deposited on aluminum chips bound for recycling in order to improve their storage stability. In addition, chips were etched with NaOH for varying amounts of time to further increase hydrophobicity through increased roughness as well as to create more binding sites for the phosphonic acids. Adsorption is confirmed via FTIR and XPS. Water contact angle measurements show the highest hydrophobicity for ODPA‐coated chips, followed by the bare substrate and MDPA coatings. As a side effect, it is also found that ODPA coatings and MDPA coatings, to a lesser extent, reduce friction within the bulk material. However, the presence of ODPA, especially in combination with etching, deteriorates the mechanical performance of the recycled product, making the removal of the molecule prior to recycling vital. Other pretreatments have next to no influence on the mechanical properties of the recyclates.
doi:10.1080/21870764.2026.2735208: Aerosol deposition (AD) enables room-temperature fabrication of polymer ceramic composites, yet the deposition mechanism of ceramic particles onto polymers is not fully understood. In this study, we investigate the growth of TiO2 films deposited by AD on polycarbonate (PC), polyamide 6 (PA6), and high-density polyethylene (HDPE), with steel as a reference material. Key process parameters (gas flow rate, number of scans, scanning velocity, and nozzle-substrate distance) are varied. Film thickness, surface roughness, and cross-section morphology (prepared by focused ion beam milling) are analyzed by laser scanning microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy. The results reveal pronounced differences between polymer and steel substrates and between the various polymers. Faster initial film growth on PC compared to PA6 and HDPE suggests that further thermal and mechanical substrate properties besides hardness, e.g. the glass transition temperature Tg and the toughness of the substrate, affect the deposition process. Furthermore, polymer substrates exhibit a non-linear dependence of film thickness on gas flow, indicating a narrower deposition window than on steel, especially in the early stages of film formation.
doi:10.7240/jeps.1904563: In this study, the morphological change of the nanofilms composed of dielectric Ca2NaNb4O13- two-dimensional nanosheets prepared via the single-droplet assembly method was investigated as a function of thermal treatment (room temperature to 450°C). The surface parameters, arithmetic mean roughness (Sa), root mean square height (Sq), Sq/Sa ratio, and slope distribution, were determined from Atomic Force Microscopy images. Based on the Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn’s tests, the heat treatment had a significant effect on the surface morphology of the nanofilms. The Sq/Sa ratio reached at 350°C (1.97 ± 0.33, p < 0.001) indicated that the temporary morphological irregularity. Conversely, the heat treatment at 450°C produced the most uniform surface with the lowest roughness (Sa = 2.75 ± 0.89) and a reduced slope distribution (mean slope of 3.15°, p < 0.001). These findings clearly indicate that the heat treatment at 450°C plays an important role in the successful fabrication of high-quality, dielectric nanofilms for next-generation nano-electronic applications.
doi:10.1016/j.surfin.2026.110789: ABSTRACT In this article we provide a comprehensive analysis of the preparation steps of polystyrene monolayer colloidal lithography for its specific use in bottom-up fabrication of ordered arrays of semiconductor nanowires. To achieve a targeted structure of selective area grown GaN nanowires by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy (PAMBE), monolayer colloidal lithography on commercial (0001)GaN-on-sapphire pseudo-substrates was implemented. First, we study the influence of the spin-coating parameters (speed and time) on the ordering of polystyrene colloids into a compact monolayer with highly regular hexagonal close-packed ordering on the underlying three-layer PSS/PDDA/PSS polyelectrolyte. Second, we provide a detailed insight into reduction of polystyrene colloids’ diameters as a function of time exposure to oxygen plasma, by applying a simple volumetric model and then by experimentally validating it. Third, we analyze Ti mask fabrication by electron-beam evaporation, addressing two critical aspects: the removal of the organic remains from the sample surface and influence of the mask thickness on the overall nanowire fabrication process. Finally, we fabricate ordered hexagonal arrays of GaN nanowires, with ≈200 nm diameter and ≈300 nm pitch. We show that the extension of the GaN nanowire array is limited by the proper ordering of colloids into a monolayer on the underlying PSS/PDDA/PSS polyelectrolyte, during the spin-coating step and we find these areas to be, at most ≈800×800 μm 2 . Next, we show that the nanowire domains with highly ordered hexagonal arrangement and high size uniformity, are predominantly limited by the size dispersion of the employed colloids, estimating the size of these areas to reach at best ≈10×10 μm 2 . High resolution transmission electron microscopy on representative GaN nanowires obtained by PAMBE confirms nearly perfect wurtzite crystalline structure with Ga-polarity. Low-temperature photoluminescence measurements on nanowire ensembles further confirm their exceptional crystal quality with (Si⁰,X A ) exciton as narrow as 286 μeV and show that numerous surface treatments involved in their fabrication do not compromise their chemical purity. We identify two key properties of GaN material, the intrinsic self-nucleation ability and strong growth anisotropy along its polar crystal direction, as key enablers for successful nanowire fabrication with this method, offering thus a roadmap for extending this bottom-up approach to…
doi:10.1016/j.jallcom.2026.191227: The microstructure and discharge behavior of the Al-5.5Zn-1.0Mg-0.04In-0.05Ti-0.04Sn alloy were regulated by heat treatment with different cooling rates. As the cooling rate after heat treatment decreases from water cooling to furnace cooling, the amount and the size of the deposited Sn-rich phases and MgZn 2 second phases increase, and the distribution of the second phases becomes more uniform due to the sufficient diffusion of the alloying elements. The homogeneous microstructure and composition of the alloy with furnace cooling enhance the discharge homogeneity. Moreover, the dispersively precipitated second phase served as an activation site, accelerating the shedding of discharge products as well as the discharge activity. The continuous dissolution of the alloy and the efficient detachment of the discharge product reduce the current loss caused by the block effect. Thus, the current efficiency of the Al-5.5Zn-1.0Mg-0.04In-0.05Ti-0.04Sn alloy increased from 83.5% to 90.1% after heat treatment with furnace cooling. Cooling rate positively correlates with reduced secondary phase precipitation (furnace < air < water cooling). The micro-galvanic corrosion between the secondary phases and the Al matrix is mitigated, resulting in improved corrosion resistance. The average corrosion rate of the Al-5.5Zn-1.0Mg-0.04In-0.05Ti-0.04Sn alloy decreases from 0.205 mm to 0.146 mm per year after heat treatment with water cooling, and the self-corrosion current density reduces from 22.17 to 18.36 μA·cm⁻ 2 , accompanied by a crystallographic preferred orientation shift from the Al(220) to the more corrosion-resistant Al(111) plane.
doi:10.48550/arxiv.2609.31333: Ultrashort X-ray pulses, as provided by X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs), offer unique opportunities to probe the formation of laser-induced nanostructures with sizes even below the optical diffraction limit, with sub-micometer and sub-picosecond spatial and temporal resolution. Using ultrafast small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), we probe the formation of nanoscatterers and nanocracks in reciprocal space as they evolve into different types of laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) on silica films. Our focus is on the dynamics and evolution of nanoscatterers and high spatial frequency LIPSS (HSFL), with spatial periods below 100 nm. Our experiments include an in-situ analysis of the pulse-by-pulse evolution of HSFL at a fixed sample location, as well as fs time-resolved delay and fluence scans using an ultrafast pump-probe scheme. We find that nanoscatterers and periodic nanocracks form at delay times of hundreds of picoseconds and subsequently evolve into HSFL. At low laser fluences, inter-pulse incubation effects become important during multi-pulse irradiation. Simultaneously, inter-pulse feedback leads to an ordering and improve the regularity of the HSFL. The experiments are complemented by theoretical analyses, including numerical Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) simulations. These combined analyses allow us to propose a five-stage model of LIPSS formation on silica films upon irradiation with fs-laser pulses.
doi:10.26599/jac.2026.9221383: Abstract Projection micro-stereolithography (PmSL) enables individualized zirconia ceramic restorations with complex freeform geometries and hundred-micrometre-scale thicknesses However, PmSL-printed ceramics often retain residual porosity, interlayer heterogeneity, and printing-induced defects after debinding, which limits full densification by conventional pressureless sintering. This limitation is particularly critical for ultrathin veneers because their reduced load-bearing thickness and intricate anatomical geometries increase sensitivity to residual pores, layer defects, and dimensional deviations. Although higher sintering temperatures can promote diffusion-driven densification, they also accelerate grain coarsening, which is detrimental to 5Y-ZrO2 ceramics with limited transformation-toughening capability. Here, an isotropic pressure-assisted densification (iPAD) strategy was developed to regulate densification, defect chemistry, and microstructural uniformity in PmSL-printed 5Y-ZrO2 ceramics. In this process, the PµSL-printed specimens were first pre-sintered and then further densified at elevated temperature under isotropic argon pressure to promote residual-pore closure and improve the overall properties of the ceramics. The optimized iPAD-treated ceramics achieved a relative density of 98.90%, together with a flexural strength of 951.30 ± 71.05 MPa, a Vickers hardness of 13.60 ± 0.07 GPa, a fracture toughness of 4.06 ± 0.30 MPa×m1/2 and a transmittance of 56.15 ± 1.11% at 555 nm. XPS, EPR, TEM, and nanoindentation analyses reveal that the complete iPAD route results in a lower relative abundance of oxygen-vacancy-related defect states, reduces defect-related scattering centers, and improves nanoscale mechanical uniformity. For ~80 µm zirconia veneers, iPAD increased the fracture load by approximately 35% while maintaining high manufacturing accuracy. This work provides a defect-regulated densification paradigm for high-reliability PmSL-printed 5Y-ZrO2 ultrathin dental veneers.
doi:10.1002/ece2.70133: ABSTRACT Potassium‐ion batteries offer a cost‐effective and sustainable alternative to large‐scale energy storage, yet electrolyte design remains a critical bottleneck. Here, we introduce a UV‐cured gel‐polymer electrolyte (GPE) that exploits bio‐derived lignin microparticles as a key functional component (as a microfiller) in potassium batteries. Far beyond acting as a passive additive, the microsized lignin phase actively engineers the polymer network, suppressing crystallinity, unlocking high chain mobility, reinforcing mechanical integrity, and enabling fast and homogeneous K + transport. Combined with ureidopyrimidinone methacrylate, polycaprolactone diol di‐methacrylate, and polyethylene glycol, and plasticized by a potassium‐based liquid electrolyte, this architecture yields an ionic conductivity that surpasses conventional separators swollen with liquid electrolyte. The resulting GPE delivers 134 mAh·g −1 at 0.1 A·g −1 with 100% retention over 1000 cycles, and introduces the first self‐healing electrolyte ever reported for potassium batteries, maintaining 86% capacity after intentional membrane damage. By demonstrating that lignin microstructuring is a powerful and unexplored design lever for K‐ion electrolytes, this work opens new possible routes toward safe, high‐performance, and long‐lived potassium batteries for stationary applications.
doi:10.3390/polym18192326: CMP (Chemical Mechanical Polishing) is essential for achieving the desired surface quality and planarity required for subsequent layers and processing steps in semiconductor manufacturing. However, the aggregation of slurry particles caused by abrasive materials can lead to scratches, defects, and increased surface roughness, degrading the quality and durability of the finished surface during the CMP process. In this study, ceria slurry was prepared using an anionic polymer dispersant with an ammonium salt of an acrylate copolymer (AAPD) at different contents of 2.5, 3.0, 5.0, and 7.0 wt.% to minimize particle aggregation and to evaluate the polysilicon (Poly-Si) film removal suppression functionality commonly required in CMP processes. The CMP evaluation revealed that the HDP MRR (material removal rate) ranged from 580 to 660 Å/min at 60 s, while the Poly-Si MRR was significantly lower at 62 to 71 Å/min, confirming the existence of Poly-Si film removal suppression behavior. The substantially reduced Poly-Si MRR suggests that AAPD may contribute to polymer-mediated suppression of Poly-Si removal, although the specific inhibition mechanism remains to be clarified. This suggests that the AAPD enables the formulation of a one-component ceria slurry with effective Poly-Si film removal suppression capability for semiconductor CMP applications.
doi:10.1088/2057-1976/aeaba8: Abstract Human cortical bone is a hierarchically organized multiphase biological nanocomposite composed primarily of type I collagen fibrils reinforced by mineralized hydroxyapatite. Although bone piezoelectricity has been recognized for decades, the quantitative determination of its effective nanoscale electromechanical coefficient and the relative contributions of organic and mineral phases remain incompletely resolved. In this work, the electromechanical response of human cortical bone was investigated using piezoresponse force microscopy. Measurements were conducted on intact cortical bone and on specimens subjected to controlled NaOCl treatment to selectively reduce the organic matrix, enabling phase-sensitive comparison. The effective electromechanical response of intact cortical bone was found to lie in the sub-picometer-per-volt range, whereas the mineral-dominated, deproteinized structure exhibited a markedly reduced response approaching the symmetry-limited behavior of centrosymmetric hydroxyapatite, with near-zero effective coefficients under dual AC resonance tracking conditions ( d 33 , eff = − 0.0138 ± 0.0074 pm V −1 ). The inferred piezoelectric coefficient associated with the collagen component was estimated to lie within the range of approximately 0.2–0.4 pm V −1 , which is in qualitative agreement with previously reported nanoscale measurements of isolated collagen fibrils, although the values obtained here are lower, likely due to differences in experimental conditions, sample preparation, and measurement sensitivity. These results provide quantitative experimental evidence that collagen is the principal contributor to electromechanical coupling in cortical bone and clarify the physical basis of load-induced bioelectric phenomena relevant to bone adaptation and regenerative biomaterials design.
doi:10.1021/acsomega.6c02180: Abstract This study presents a comparative evaluation of three strategies for hydrophobizing glass surfaces: direct surface silanization with dimethyldichlorosilane (DMDClSi), the application of a hybrid silica coating (H-SiO2), and the use of a hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS)-modified silica coating (P-SiO2/HMDS). The glass/H-SiO2 and glass/P-SiO2/HMDS coatings were prepared by a sol–gel process and deposited onto glass substrates via dip-coating using alcohol-based precursor sols. All surface treatments resulted in hydrophobic surfaces, with advancing water contact angles exceeding 90° and very low contact angle hysteresis (∼1°), indicating uniform and stable water-repellent surfaces. Surface free energy analysis confirmed the predominantly nonpolar character of the modified surfaces, with the lowest values observed for the DMDClSi-treated samples (18 ± 1 mN m–1). Both silica-based coatings also increased the light transmittance of the glass substrates compared to the bare glass, achieving maximum transmittance (Tmax) of ≈99.6–99.7% and average transmittance increases of 6.0–6.5% (400–800 nm), together with controlled porosity (34–35%) and uniform thickness values (127 nm). Ellipsometric porosimetry revealed marked differences in pore structures between the silica-based coatings: the glass/H-SiO2 coating exhibited a high-surface-area porous network (1124 m2 cm–3, 38% porosity), whereas the glass/P-SiO2/HMDS coating showed higher porosity (48%) with larger mesopores and a lower specific surface area (245 m2 cm–3), indicating a more open porous structure. The stability of hydrophobic and optical properties was investigated under combined chemical and thermal stress using a three-factor Box–Behnken design. The results identified pH as the main degradation parameter, while temperature and exposure time acted as accelerating factors. Under alkaline–thermal conditions, degradation of Si–CH3 groups was identified as the primary mechanism responsible for hydrophobic failure in the glass/H-SiO2 system, as confirmed by ATR-FTIR analysis. These results suggest that the high-surface-area pore network of the glass/H-SiO2 coating is more susceptible to the loss of Si–CH3 functionalities. Wettability measurements demonstrated that the glass/DMDClSi surface exhibited the highest resistance to degradation throughout the investigated design space. Among the silica-based coatings, the glass/P-SiO2/HMDS sample showed markedly improved hydrophobic stability compared to…
doi:10.1002/smll.75662: ABSTRACT Practical implementation of two‐dimensional (2D) transition‐metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) in novel optoelectronics requires a fundamental understanding of carrier dynamics and interfacial states at 2D/3D heterostructures. Herein, a mixed‐dimensional p‐n junction based on monolayer tungsten disulfide () and cuprous oxide () is investigated. An anomalous emission (AE) at 1.66 eV is identified at room temperature, which is in the same spectral range as oxygen‐related defect luminescence, but is enhanced at the heterointerface under 457 nm excitation. While this sub‐bandgap feature resembles the spectral signature of an interlayer exciton (ILX), its combined excitation‐wavelength, power, temperature, and bias dependence suggests that the emission is predominantly defect‐mediated and modified by the / interface. External modulation of the AE intensity is demonstrated via vertical bias, yielding an approximately 45% maximum‐to‐minimum modulation of the normalized AE/ PL area ratio over the applied bias range from V to V at 93 K. This modulation is asymmetric, showing a correlation between AE quenching and photocurrent generation under reverse bias. The spectral response peaks near the open‐circuit condition, marking a regime of efficient carrier accumulation and interfacial trapping. These findings identify / as a model hybrid interface for probing electrically tunable defect‐mediated recombination in mixed‐dimensional heterostructures.
doi:10.1016/j.rineng.2026.113128: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) have been widely applied in military, agricultural, and environmental monitoring fields, becoming an essential component of advanced technological systems. However, traditional UAV often face the dual challenges of heavy component weight and complex structural design in manufacturing, which limits their performance and application range. Proposed in this paper is a self-folding UAV architecture enabled by thermally responsive 4D printing strategies, which achieves programmable shape transformation of the airframe structures and propellers through the stimulus-responsive characteristics of shape memory polymers (SMPs) and computer-aided path design. Finite element analysis and aerodynamic simulations verified the optimization of the UAV's structural design and aerodynamic performance. Comparative experiments further confirmed the enhanced propulsion performance of the 4D-printed propeller blades, which generated a thrust of 0.155 N, approximately four times higher than that of the conventional 3D-printed blades under the tested operating conditions. The fully assembled UAV prototype, with a total mass of approximately 45 g, generated a total lift of approximately 0.58 N and achieved a flight endurance of 7.5 min. This study provides an innovative theoretical framework and empirical foundation for the development of the next generation of lightweight, highly portable, and rapidly deployable adaptive UAV systems.
doi:10.1016/j.carbon.2026.122139: ABSTRACT Understanding the relationships between synthesis conditions, defect chemistry, and electrochemical properties is essential for the rational design of advanced carbon nanomaterials. Herein, the thermally triggered and dopant-mediated evolution of hierarchically branched boron/nitrogen heterodoped carbon nanowalls (BCNWs) grown by microwave plasma-enhanced chemical vapour deposition is systematically investigated by varying substrate temperature, methane concentration, and the gas-phase nitrogen-to-carbon ratio. Among the investigated parameters, substrate temperature is identified as the dominant factor governing nanoarchitectural evolution, driving the transition from densely packed nanowalls with a higher sp 3 contribution to highly branched, graphitic sp 2 -rich frameworks. Combined Raman, XPS, SIMS, and EELS reveal distinct boron and nitrogen incorporation pathways, with boron preferentially stabilising ordered sp 2 domains, while nitrogen is mainly incorporated into pyridinic defect sites without complete electronic compensation between the dopants. The resulting temperature-dependent evolution of defect chemistry is directly reflected in the electrochemical properties of the materials. Electrochemical characterisation demonstrates fast electron-transfer kinetics for all BCNWs, whereas the BCNW 0.5N-800°C-12% electrode exhibits the largest electrochemically accessible surface area and the highest response toward bisphenol A as a model emerging pollutant. These findings establish direct links between plasma-assisted growth, heteroatom incorporation, structural evolution, and electrochemical performance, providing design principles for next-generation carbon electrochemical interfaces.
doi:10.1002/apxr.70193: ABSTRACT In this work, a combined experimental and modeling study of strain effects on the radiative emission of Ge quantum dots (QDs) grown on Si nanotips (NTs) is presented. Pure germanium QDs with heights of 30 and 70 nm are deposited on top of Si NTs using solid‐source molecular beam epitaxy. The micro‐photoluminescence measurements show a blueshift of the peak emission from to eV as the QD height increases from 30 to 70 nm, respectively. To understand this effect, strain in Ge QDs and Si NTs is analyzed using X‐ray diffraction. An in‐plane compressive strain of % is observed in the Ge QDs, while the Si NT substrate exhibits an in‐plane tensile strain of about 2.9 %. Furthermore, the electronic band structure calculations employing single‐band method coupled to the computation of the elastic strain tensor using continuum elasticity are performed. The results indicate that the unusual size dependence of Ge QD emission is due to a combination of (i) strain in Ge QDs, (ii) prominence of ‐direct electron–hole transitions for larger Ge QDs over ‐indirect ones more frequent in smaller dots. Finally, transitions involving electrons and heavy‐ and light‐hole states are identified.
doi:10.1016/j.hybadv.2026.100749: The valorisation of industrial by-products into sustainable construction materials has attracted considerable research interest; however, the relationship between alkali-activated gel formation, microstructural evolution, and thermo-electrical transport behaviour remains insufficiently understood. In this study, alkali-activated cementitious paver blocks were developed using ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) as the primary aluminosilicate precursor and 100% copper slag (CS100%) as the fine aggregate under ambient curing with a low-alkalinity activator (3 M NaOH). The intrinsic thermo-electrical transport properties were evaluated using powdered specimens (<600 μm) prepared from hardened paver blocks, whereas the compressive strength and microstructural characterisation were performed on intact paver-blocks. The GGBS + CS100% system was compared to conventional ordinary Portland cement (OPC) + manufactured sand (MS) system. Microstructural analyses revealed the formation of a dense, predominantly amorphous C-(N)-A-S-H-rich aluminosilicate gel network with refined pore architecture and enhanced particle connectivity. Consequently, the GGBS + CS100% composite achieved a 60-day compressive strength of 72.35 MPa, representing an approximately 24% improvement over the OPC + MS (58.45 MPa). The corresponding powdered composite exhibited lower thermal conductivity (0.209 W/mK) and electrical conductivity (0.7516 mS/cm) than the OPC + MS counterpart (0.225 W/mK and 1.044 mS/cm, respectively). The reduced transport trends were attributed to the formation of highly polymerised aluminosilicate gel network, reduced ionic mobility, and increased resistance to heat and ionic transport. These findings establish a clear structure–property relationship and demonstrate that alkali-activated GGBS–copper slag composites are promising sustainable paving materials that combine high mechanical strength, improved electrical insulation, and acceptable heat-transfer properties.
doi:10.1002/pssa.70538: A method for obtaining luminescent diamond nanoparticles doped with germanium from nanocrystalline diamond (NCD) films grown by microwave plasma‐assisted chemical vapor deposition (MPCVD) is presented. Thermal etching in the presence of an alkali metal nitrate enables the selective disruption of intercrystallite boundaries, resulting in the formation of individual particles without mechanical grinding. Structural and morphological characterization by scanning and transmission electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and dynamic light scattering reveals the formation of particles with characteristic sizes down to ~100 nm, along with a minor fraction of larger microcrystals. The particles retain the crystalline quality of the parent film and exhibit photoluminescence associated with Ge‐V and Si‐V centers. Second‐order correlation measurements reveal single‐photon emission from a minority of Ge‐V‐related diffraction‐limited spots, demonstrating the presence of isolated optically active Ge‐V emitters in the nanoparticle sample. The proposed approach provides a scalable route for producing luminescent diamond nanoparticles for photonic and quantum applications.
doi:10.3762/bjnano.17.87: The microstructure, transport, and galvanometric properties of Ni 48 Fe 12 Cr 40 thin films of various thickness, obtained by magnetron sputtering, were studied in the temperature range of 93–293 K. The Ni 48 Fe 12 Cr 40 film with thickness of 5 nm has been found to be X-ray amorphous and exhibits a negative temperature coefficient of resistance. The observation of anisotropic magnetoresistance, as well as anomalous and planar Hall effect, indicates the presence of ferromagnetic ordering in this sample. The increase of the Ni 48 Fe 12 Cr 40 film thickness to 8 nm leads to the crystallization and texture formation, which promotes more uniform distribution of Cr atoms in Ni–Fe matrix and suppression of the long-range ferromagnetic order.
doi:10.1016/j.bioactmat.2026.06.017: The integrative regeneration of articular cartilage and subchondral bone remains a major clinical challenge due to the difficulties of mimicking the spatial and compositional complexity of native osteochondral tissues in artificial implants. To overcome these limitations, 3D printing has enabled personalized solutions, going beyond traditional plug-shaped scaffolds that are limited to repairing small, cylindrical focal defects. In this study, we report solvent-free 4D printing of olive oil-derived fatty amide-based acrylate photoresin for osteochondral tissue engineering applications. The physicochemical properties of the printed polymers were fine-tuned using acrylic acid as a comonomer. With optimized printing conditions, the resin can be printed into high-resolution objects with each layer of ∼50-100 μm. Depending on the resin composition, the mechanical properties of the printed polymers vary between ∼200-1400 kPa with ∼210-420% strain under tensile setting, and ∼26-98 MPa at ∼80% strain under compressive setting. The mechanical properties of the printed polymers are comparable to those of various interfacial soft tissues, including ligaments, articular cartilage, and soft collagenous bone, indicating their potential for interfacial tissue engineering applications. Furthermore, the printed polymers showed near-body temperature-responsive shape memory (4D) properties with a recovery ratio of ∼99% for optimized resin composition. In addition, the printed polymers exhibited excellent bactericidal antimicrobial activity against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, highlighting their multifunctional nature. More importantly, the printed polymers exhibited good cytocompatibility (cell viability ∼≥90% across all samples compared to control) toward adipose-derived human mesenchymal stem cells, facilitating growth factor-free osteogenic and chondrogenic differentiation, which confirms their potential for osteochondral tissue regeneration. Overall, the newly developed biobased resin offers a low-cost, sustainable alternative for 4D printing of personalized implants for osteochondral tissue regeneration.
doi:10.1016/j.mbplus.2026.100205: Marfan syndrome (MFS) is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused by mutations in the gene encoding fibrillin-1 ( FBN1 ), the main component of extracellular microfibrils. In the aortic wall, these microfibrils maintain structural integrity and sustain hemodynamic load. Pathogenic FBN1 variants are thought to structurally and functionally impair fibrillin-1 microfibrils, leading to progressive aortic aneurysm and dissection, the major causes of morbidity and mortality in MFS. However, the molecular mechanisms whereby these genetic variants translate into structural and mechanical defects are far from being understood. Here we explored the morphology and the nanomechanical characteristics of individual aortic fibrillin-1 microfibrils from MFS patients and non-MFS controls by atomic force microscopy. The topographical assessment revealed a preserved overall pattern and periodicity of the microfibrils, but with morphological irregularities in MFS microfibril beads and interbead segments, consistent with presumed structural fragility. Force spectroscopy revealed a reduction of transverse elastic modulus in patients harboring haploinsufficient FBN1 variants. Nanoindentation analysis was indicative of localized deformation, occurring at markedly lower forces in MFS microfibril beads, suggesting diminished load-bearing capacity. These data provide direct nanoscale evidence of structural and mechanical consequences of FBN1 mutations on human aortic tissue. Altered fibrillin-1 microfibril morphology and reduced stiffness in MFS support a pathogenetic mechanism in which compromised microfibrillar integrity weakens the aortic wall, predisposing it to progressive dilation.
doi:10.1111/jerd.70235: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of periodic repolishing on the surface and mechanical properties of resin-based CAD/CAM materials subjected to combined mechanical cycling and simulated toothbrushing, with or without periodic repolishing. Methods Two resin-based CAD/CAM materials were investigated (Tetric CAD [TC] and Shofu HC [SH]). Groups (n = 12) were assigned according to the evaluation period and repolishing (RPL) condition. The aging protocol comprised simulated toothbrushing (ST-200 g load, 250 cycles/min) combined with mechanical cycling (MC-50 N load, 1.67 Hz frequency) performed in aging intervals (AI-2.4 × 10 5 MC + 10,000 ST), totaling two periods (5 × AI and 10 × AI). Periodic repolishing was performed using a clinical polishing system (OptraGloss, Diamond High-Gloss polisher [HP]). Surface roughness (Ra), Vickers microhardness (VH), flexural strength (FS), and elastic modulus (EM) were quantitatively evaluated, while SEM and AFM analyses were performed qualitatively. Data normality and homogeneity were verified, followed by two-way ANOVA and Tukey's post hoc test (α = 0.05). Results Aging significantly increased surface roughness and reduced microhardness in both resin-based CAD/CAM materials (p 1RPL and T 2RPL ) showed higher VH and lower Ra values (p 1 and T 2 ). No significant differences in FS or EM were observed after aging (p = 0.664 and 0.185, respectively). Conclusion Aging significantly affected the surface roughness and microhardness of both materials. Periodic repolishing proved to be an effective strategy for minimizing the effects of aging, thereby reducing surface roughness and preserving microhardness. Clinical significance Intraoral repolishing at yearly recall intervals may help control surface degradation, maintain smoother surfaces, and preserve microhardness over time, particularly for indirect restorations fabricated from resin-based CAD/CAM materials.
doi:10.1039/d6ra07333f: Multifunctional organic-inorganic materials are promising candidates for next-generation optoelectronic devices. This study reports the design, characterization, and device application of a copper-based pyranoquinoline complex, Cu(HMDPQ), with enhanced optoelectronic performance. Structural analysis confirmed a square-planar geometry with bidentate oxygen coordination. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations using the 6-311G(d,p) basis set supported the experimental findings, revealing an energy gap of 2.86 eV and a pronounced nonlinear optical (NLO) response attributed to efficient intramolecular charge transfer. Thin films showed uniform morphology, an average grain size of 80.3 nm, and low surface roughness (∼8.5 nm), favoring charge transport. Optical studies revealed dual direct band gaps (1.81 and 1.93 eV), strong blue emission, and lower-energy transitions from metal-ligand interactions. A metal/organic/semiconductor heterojunction exhibited rectifying behavior, low dark current (∼1.6 × 10 -8 A cm -2 ), a barrier height of ∼1.05 eV, responsivity of 3.7 × 10 -2 A W -1 , and detectivity of 5.2 × 10 11 Jones, demonstrating potential for photodetector and temperature-sensing applications.
doi:10.3390/ma19204379: This study investigates the feasibility of enhancing graphene-coated para-aramid yarn's resistance to pull-out from fabric structures, measured by junction rupture force (JRF), by increasing the fibre surface roughness with nano- and microstructures obtained by laser irradiation and graphene coating. Two types of Kevlar ® KM2 fibre woven fabrics were subjected to continuous wave CO 2 laser processing to investigate the influence of laser power and scanning speed combinations on yarn pull-out force from the fabric structure under fixed laser spot diameter and raster step. Depending on the combination of applied laser parameters, a JRF increase of between 32% and 99% was achieved for laser-irradiated KM2+440 fabric compared to the JRF of untreated fabric. Applying a single layer of graphene coating to the fabric pretreated with optimal laser parameters doubled the JRF increase. When a second layer was applied, the increase tripled, indicating that cumulative effects were produced. As a result of laser treatment, the V2KM2600_laz variant's JRF increased by 27% compared to the unmodified fabric, while the corresponding JRF difference for V3KM2600_laz was statistically insignificant, and any further JRF increase for V3 was only provided by the graphene coating layers. Meanwhile, for the laser-modified V2KM2600_laz, the JRF increase for the first graphene layer reached 56%, and adding a second graphene layer boosted it to 90%. The AFM and SEM imaging studies of the self-organization of nano- and microstructures on the surface of Kevlar ® KM2 fibres allowed us to conclude that irradiation-induced structures formed in the defect-enriched upper nanolayer of the 300-350 nm thick fibre skin, with a thickness of about 8 nm. Therefore, treatment within the examined laser parameter limits does not affect the fibres' core structure.
doi:10.1021/acsnano.6c10214: Performance of tandem junction nanowire (NW) solar cells relies on the electronic quality of the tunnel diodes which serve as the separating junctions between subcells. Yet, the relevant interfacial physics occurs below the optical diffraction limit. Here we use hyperspectral tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS) to map, with nanoscale precision, axially defined heterojunctions in InP/InGaP tandem junction photovoltaic NWs. By resolving mode-specific phonon and phonon-plasmon responses, we show that the nominally abrupt p/p++ and p++/n++ junctions are compositionally graded. The TOM mode, used as the primary compositional marker, yields transition widths of ∼90-120 nm, whereas other lattice- and carrier-sensitive modes exhibit broader central widths up to ∼190 nm, reflecting their additional sensitivity to alloying, structural disorder, and electronic coupling. In a first-order approximation, rescaling these TERS-derived widths to shorter, device-relevant NWs yields narrower junctions, consistent with independent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements that qualitatively capture the same trend despite surface and tip convolution effects. Complementary equilibrium band-edge model combined with a simplified one-dimensional Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) calculation, as an illustrative trend, further indicates that such grading is expected to widen the effective tunnel barrier. These findings establish mode-selective hyperspectral TERS as a validated, noninvasive method for quantitative nanoscale mapping of compositional grading in III-V NW junctions, with the carrier-sensitive L1 phonon-plasmon response providing complementary, model-assisted insight into the electronic evolution of the junctions.
doi:10.1126/sciadv.aej6501: Accurate determination of carrier density and mobility is fundamental to understanding the transport physics of conducting polymers and optimizing their performance. However, Hall effect measurements, widely used for determining carrier concentrations in other materials, have been of limited use for conducting polymers. Applying the conventional Hall coefficient expression ([Formula: see text]) consistently yields unphysically high carrier densities in heavily doped polymers. Here, we resolve this problem using a quasi-one-dimensional (Q1D) tight-binding model of the band structure of uniaxially aligned polymer films to analyze the p-type to n-type transition in the Hall effect observed upon increased doping. Our Q1D framework achieves excellent agreement between Hall-derived carrier densities and other independent measurements over a wide doping range. Our findings indicate that the transport physics of aligned polymers is governed by the topology of a single Q1D band within a simple band-filling framework and establish Hall measurements as a powerful tool for studying their charge transport physics.
doi:10.1039/d6ra07963f: High-performance nanofiltration (NF) membranes are essential for sustainable water treatment but are often limited by the permeability-fouling trade-off. In this study, highly crystalline sub-25 nm NH 2 -MIL-101(Cr) nanoparticles (19-21 nm), possessing a high BET surface area (1700.18 m 2 g -1 ) and permanent pores (2.04 nm), were hydrothermally synthesized and incorporated into polysulfone (PSF) mixed matrix membranes via phase inversion. The uniform distribution of hydrophilic NH 2 groups enhanced membrane hydrophilicity, reducing the water contact angle from 76.2 ± 2° to 56.1 ± 2° at the optimum loading of 0.75 wt%. At 5 bar using a 2000 ppm feed solution, the optimized membrane achieved a water flux of 15.3 kg m -2 h -1 , representing a 2.3-fold increase over pristine PSF, while maintaining high rejection of MgSO 4 (86.5%) and CaSO 4 (96.2%) through combined steric hindrance and Donnan exclusion mechanisms. Flux increased linearly with pressure up to 17.8 kg m -2 h -1 at 7.0 bar. Organic fouling tests with 10 ppm humic acid demonstrated excellent antifouling performance, with flux recovery ratios of 83.2% and 68.5% after the first and second alkaline cleaning cycles, respectively. These findings demonstrate that the PSF/NH 2 -MIL-101(Cr) mixed matrix membrane effectively overcomes the permeability-fouling trade-off, offering a promising platform for high-performance and long-term desalination applications.
doi:10.1039/d6sm00371k: DNA origami is a powerful method to achieve nanoscale folded structures. DNA origami is typically employed to create precisely and tightly folded objects often in small quantities and studied at single molecule scale. Here, we use the DNA origami method to design and fold polymers with complex topologies, and study their rheology and viscoelastic properties in dense conditions. First, we designed and purified topologically distinct DNA nanostructures - linear, circular, and "tadpole" polymers - to evaluate how polymer architecture influences entanglement and rheology. Despite their distinct topologies, we observe that all constructs obeyed universal rheological scalings, likely due to their short length. However, upon thermal annealing in the bulk, the DNA polymers displayed significantly different behaviours. Our results suggest that DNA polymers could be used to engineer thermoresponsive behaviours in complex fluids by introducing reversible and topology-dependent crosslinking.
doi:10.1039/d6ra06516c: Hen egg yolk is an essential component of food items such as mayonnaise and salad dressing. Phosvitin (PVT) is a phosphoprotein that exists in the granules of hen egg yolk and stabilizes food emulsions by preventing phase separation. Understanding how this protein is adsorbed at the interface of water and an edible oil in the presence and absence of lipids is essential. To monitor the kinetics of this adsorption, the dynamic interfacial tension was determined in the current investigation. The drop in interfacial tension over time indicates the adsorption of protein at the interface, which is enhanced upon increasing the concentration of protein in the water phase. However, at higher concentrations, the positive activation energy hinders the adsorption process, resulting in saturation of the interfacial tension. Dilational rheology of the macromolecular film at this oil-water interface shows the elastic nature of the film to be greater than its viscous nature, indicating the formation of a soft gel film. Low concentrations of the zwitterionic lipid 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl- sn -glycero-3-phosphocholine (POPC) promote the adsorption of this protein at the interface. Interestingly, at high concentration, the lipid overtakes the interface, removing the protein from it. The lipid-protein composite film again shows a soft gel nature. AFM images provided evidence of PVT-POPC assembly, revealing distinct morphological features associated with lipid-induced reorganization of the protein at the interface.
